articles.title: El intenso cara a cara de Jefferson Lerma con Alexis Mac Allister
articles.standfirst: Jefferson Lerma y Alexis Mac Allister protagonizaron un picante cruce en la Premier League
articles.summary: Jefferson Lerma y Alexis Mac Allister protagonizaron un picante cruce en la Premier League
articles.body: El duelo entre el Crystal Palace y el Liverpool en el Selhurst Park Stadium dejó mucho más que los tres puntos para los 'reds'. Más allá de la derrota 1-3 de las 'águilas' y de la difícil situación del equipo londinense en la parte baja de la tabla de la Premier League, uno de los momentos que más encendió las redes sociales y los corrillos de la prensa internacional fue el intenso cara a cara protagonizado por el colombiano Jefferson Lerma y el mediocampista argentino Alexis Mac Allister. El partido estuvo marcado por la alta intensidad propia del fútbol inglés. Por un lado, el volante de la Selección Colombia, Jefferson Lerma, quien disputó todo el encuentro —incluso desempeñándose en labores defensivas complejas—, batalló cada pelota dividida en el centro del campo y la zona posterior. Por el otro, el campeón del mundo Alexis Mac Allister, autor del primer tanto del compromiso a los 39 minutos, impuso condiciones en la medular del equipo dirigido por Arne Slot. La temperatura del juego fue escalando con el pasar de los minutos. A falta de diez minutos para el final reglamentario, la pierna fuerte hizo mella en el ambiente: ambos jugadores terminaron viendo la tarjeta amarilla en cuestión de minutos (Lerma al 81' y Mac Allister al 82') tras un roce verbal y físico que reflejó la frustración del cuadro local y la férrea disputa por cada balón. El cruce dejó patente el carácter sudamericano en la cancha, con recriminaciones mutuas, empujones y miradas desafiantes que encendieron los ánimos de los aficionados en las gradas. La tensión comenzó cuando un compañero de Mac Allister, Víctor, se quedó tendido sobre el césped pidiendo una supuesta falta por parte de Lerma Solís. La reacción del volante colombiano fue inmediata: le exigió al jugador que se levantara asegurando que no lo había tocado y que estaba fingiendo. Al escuchar los reclamos, el argentino intervino para defender a su compañero: "La situación empezó cuando Víctor se fue al suelo tras el choque. Lerma inmediatamente empezó a gritar que Víctor estaba simulando... Yo lo oí y me giré porque Víctor es mi compañero. No voy a quedarme ahí parado mientras alguien lo insulta", reveló Mac Allister en declaraciones a los medios oficiales del torneo. El mediocampista del Liverpool le reprochó a Lerma que, si creía que era simulación, debía hablar con el juez central y no faltarle al respeto a su compañero. La respuesta del colombiano fue directa: "¿Por qué te metes? Tu compañero se está ridiculizando". Para Jefferson Lerma, la jornada dominical no fue ideal. Además del encontronazo con el volante argentino de los 'reds', el mediocampista colombiano y su equipo sufrieron un duro revés que los deja complicados en la tabla de posiciones, hundiéndolos en la parte de abajo del rentado inglés. El Palace sufrió con los goles de Mac Allister, el alemán Florian Wirtz y el sueco Alexander Isak, mientras que el descuento llegó sobre el final gracias a Eddie Nketiah desde el punto penal (1-3 definitivo). Pese al panorama adverso del Crystal Palace, la actitud combativa de Lerma sigue siendo una de sus marcas registradas, llevándolo a medirse sin titubeos ante figuras de talla mundial como el propio Mac Allister en una de las ligas más competitivas del planeta.

articles.title: El golazo de Gio Moreno por el que piden su regreso del retiro
articles.standfirst: Gio Moreno y Giovanni Hernández brillan con golazo y asistencia en partido de leyendas
articles.summary: Gio Moreno y Giovanni Hernández brillan con golazo y asistencia en partido de leyendas
articles.body: El talento nunca se pierde, solo se transforma en clase pura. En un vibrante encuentro de exhibición entre leyendas de Colombia y Ecuador, dos de los enganches más exquisitos que ha dado el fútbol cafetero en las últimas décadas recordaron sus mejores épocas sobre el terreno de juego y regalaron una jugada que rápidamente se hizo viral en las redes sociales. Los protagonistas de la función fueron Giovanni 'Gio' Moreno y Giovanni Hernández, quienes demostraron que la calidad y la visión de juego se mantienen intactas a pesar del paso de los años. La jugada colectiva desató la locura de los asistentes y de los usuarios en internet. Todo comenzó en los pies de Giovanni Hernández, el recordado 'Príncipe', quien con la elegancia que lo caracterizaba en equipos como el Junior de Barranquilla, Colo Colo y la Selección Colombia, inventó un pase de lujo rompiendo líneas defensivas con una precisión milimétrica. El balón encontró receptor en Giovanni Moreno, el espigado volante creativo que dejó huella en Atlético Nacional, Racing Club y el fútbol de China. 'Gio' controló con clase y, con la frialdad y categoría de un delantero de élite, firmó un golazo que dejó sin opciones al guardameta rival. La combinación perfecta entre la pausa, la inteligencia táctica y la estética del balompié sudamericano. Acciones como esta reavivan la nostalgia de los aficionados por el fútbol de creación pura, donde la pausa, el talento y la inventiva en el mediocampo eran el motor principal de los equipos. Ver a figuras de la talla de 'Gio' Moreno y el 'Príncipe' Hernández compartir cancha y asociarse con tanta naturalidad recuerda por qué se ganaron el cariño y la admiración de todo un continente. El video de la anotación continúa circulando masivamente en plataformas digitales, y ha provocado que pidan el regreso desde su retiro por los seguidores del fútbol que disfrutan recordando la magia de los ídolos de antaño.

articles.title: Braden Mann’s 86-Yard Punt Rewrites Eagles Special Teams History
articles.summary: Braden Mann's 86-yard punt vs. Giants is the second-longest of the century. This play exposes a massive gap in NFL punting and changes the game.
articles.body:
Braden Mann kicked an 86-yard punt against the New York Giants on Sunday, marking the second-longest punt in the last 25 years. This single play put the Giants on their own six-yard line and shifted the momentum of the game. The punt occurred during Week 9 of the NFL season when the Philadelphia Eagles faced off in a defensive struggle. Fox Sports reported that this boot was the longest punt seen since 2001, ending a long dry spell for such massive kicks in the league.

The score at halftime was a tight 8-6 battle, showing just how hard both defenses fought before Mann struck. Head coach Nick Sirianni sent the punt team out for one of the final plays of the first half, and Mann delivered a perfect strike from his own end zone. After rolling out of bounds at the six-yard line, the ball first touched down near the 17-yard line with only seconds remaining in the second quarter. This specific distance ranks as the sixth-longest punt in the entire league since 1975, proving that Mann has a rare gift for distance.

Historical context makes this kick even more impressive when looking at the all-time records. The longest punt in history still belongs to Steve O'Neal, who kicked a 98-yarder with the New York Jets back in 1969. Just above Mann's recent effort was a punt by the New England Patriots' Luke Prestidge, who went 89 yards in 1984. Mann's 86-yard boot falls right between these two giants of the sport. Fox Sports noted that Mann's career-high before this game was a 72-yarder he punted in 2022 while playing for the New York Jets. This new distance exceeds his previous best by over 10 yards, a significant jump for any professional punter.

Mann is now 5-foot-11 and playing in his seventh season in the league, yet he just notched a career best that fans will talk about for years. However, this kick does not hold the record for the longest punt in Eagles history. Legendary quarterback Randall Cunningham earned that distinction with a 91-yard punt in 1989. Cunningham's record still stands, but Mann's performance on Sunday brings the team back into the conversation for the biggest kicks in franchise history. The sheer distance of the punt forced the Giants to start their next drive deep in their own territory, a nightmare scenario for any offense.

Special teams are often overlooked until a moment like this shifts the flow of a game. Since the Eagles and Giants engaged in a fierce defensive battle marked by low scoring, every yard gained on special teams became vital. Mann's ability to flip the field so drastically means the Giants' offense will have to work twice as hard to score points. This kick demonstrates that special teams can be a weapon just as potent as the offense or defense. Fox Sports highlighted that this was a wild stat for Week 9, proving that even in a league of thousands of players, one boot can define a game.

Since 1975, the 86-yard punt stands as the sixth-longest in the league.

The Eagles' big special-teams moment did not change the outcome. New York rallied after halftime behind backup quarterback Jameis Winston (who entered after J.J. McCarthy left with a hip injury) and won 19-11 at Lincoln Financial Field. Winston's 5-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Likely in the third quarter, plus four field goals from Dominic Zvada, proved decisive. Philadelphia managed only a Jake Elliott field goal after the break and fell to 2-7, extending its losing streak to seven games. The Giants improved to 5-2-1 and snapped a long home drought against the Eagles in Philadelphia.

Mann's 86-yard punt remains the clearest highlight of a low-scoring, defensive struggle. It flipped the field late in the first half and forced New York to start deep in its own territory, but the Eagles' offense never built on the advantage. For a team searching for positives in a rough season, the career-long boot from Mann stands out as a rare bright spot on an otherwise quiet afternoon at the Linc.

articles.title: LaNorris Sellers plays through ankle injury to lead South Carolina past Texas A&M
articles.summary: LaNorris Sellers was already limping when he kept the ball on an option and ran 41 yards for the touchdown that sealed the South Carolina Gamecocks’ 17-9 win...
articles.body:
LaNorris Sellers was already limping when he kept the ball on an option and ran 41 yards for the touchdown that sealed the South Carolina Gamecocks' 17-9 win over the Texas A&M Aggies on Saturday. Teammates and staff had to help him to the bench after he crossed the goal line.

Sellers had spent the end of the first half in the locker room. Texas A&M defensive end Sam M'Pemba landed on his left ankle on a strip-sack late in the second quarter, and Sellers was helped to the medical tent and then off the field for X-rays. Shane Beamer said at halftime that the team was concerned, then said the X-rays had come back negative. Sellers was on the field for South Carolina's first possession of the third quarter.

"I knew I wanted to be out there and didn't want to sit the rest of the second half knowing we had a chance to win the game, It's just fighting through the pain, honestly." Sellers said afterward.

He played the second half with little of the mobility that defines his game, and South Carolina's offense stalled for most of it. Texas A&M took a 9-7 lead on a third-quarter field goal before Malik Orsan's 43-yard kick put the Gamecocks back in front 10-9 with 8:14 to play. Sellers finished 20-of-31 for 251 yards and a touchdown, most of it on a bad ankle.

Why didn't Sellers go down short of the goal line?

South Carolina led 10-9 and needed to burn the final 87 seconds when Sellers found a lane on the option. A slide short of the end zone might have let the Gamecocks run out the clock, while the touchdown put them up eight and handed Texas A&M the ball back with a chance to tie. Sellers said the ankle made the decision for him. "I really couldn't stop (because my ankle) started hurting," Sellers said .

The defense made the score hold, and the win was South Carolina's fourth straight after a 2-3 start.

"I don't ever want to lose three games, but because of the adversity that we dealt with early in the season, maybe it helped us to find a way to win tonight," Beamer said . The Gamecocks are 6-3 and bowl eligible, with a trip to the Arkansas Razorbacks on Nov. 14.

It was a long way from the second quarter, when Sellers walked to the locker room without his cleat in the same week he collected two national player of the week awards. Former Missouri and NFL quarterback Chase Daniel was among those who reacted on X. "What a GUTSY performance by Sellers! Cockvember is here to stay!" Daniel wrote .

articles.title: Cowboys rally for 27-23 win over Colts
articles.summary: Caleb Downs' first career interception allowed the Cowboys to escape with a 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.
articles.body:
Caleb Downs' first career interception allowed the Cowboys to escape with a 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.

The Colts tied the Cowboys 20-20 on Spencer Shrader's 59-yard field goal with 5:56 remaining. The Cowboys tried to regain the lead, but Brandon Aubrey's 50-yard attempt was no good with 3:30 left.

Aubrey's miss allowed Shrader to give the Colts a 23-20 lead with 1:37 left with a 50-yard field goal.

The Cowboys then drove 65 yards in only four plays, with Ryan Flournoy catching a 46-yard pass to help set up Javonte Williams' 1-yard touchdown run with 1:08 remaining. The Colts appeared to let Williams score, so they would get the ball back.

The Colts got only as close as their own 26, though, before an intentional grounding call followed by Daniels' interception to Downs to end it.

The Cowboys are 4-5 and the Colts are 2-7, with decisions to make about the futures of Jones, Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs as the trade deadline approaches Tuesday.

The Cowboys outgained the Colts 508 to 271. But CeeDee Lamb lost a red-zone fumble on one of the craziest plays of the season; Dak Prescott lost a fumble that led to a 19-yard Colts' touchdown drive; and the Cowboys had 14 penalties for 153 yards, including a 15-yarder on DeMarvion Overshown, who is inactive but came onto the field for a celebration.

Prescott was 21-of-34 for 335 yards and two touchdowns, with Lamb catching 10 for 195 yards and a touchdown. The Cowboys played without No. 2 wide receiver George Pickens, who was inactive with a hamstring injury.

Javonte Williams rushed for 101 yards and a touchdown on 20 carries, and Tyler Goodson had 12 carries for 77 yards.

Jones was 20-of-34 for 180 yards with a touchdown and an interception in what might have been his final game as a Colt. Taylor had 13 carries for 46 yards and lost a fumble. Ashton Dulin had a 55-yard touchdown.

Josh Downs, Caleb's brother, had three catches for 24 yards.

articles.title: Kentucky tumbles to No. 13 in updated AP poll
articles.summary: The Kentucky football team took a big loss to Tennessee on Saturday, and dropped in the new AP Poll this week.
articles.body:
Some losses you carry home. Others carry you, in the dark, up the long road out of Knoxville, with the game film already replaying behind your eyelids.

Kentucky football took the second kind on Saturday night. Tennessee 34, Kentucky 6 . By Sunday the voters had finished the arithmetic. The Wildcats, No. 8 a week ago, are now No. 13 in the AP Top 25 , down five spots at 7-2. They have 897 points and the quiet of a team that learned what it is not yet.

Will Stein's ball club walked into Neyland Stadium with the SEC standings in its pocket and a chance to do what Kentucky teams have chased across generations: win in Knoxville, a place the Wildcats haven't won since 1984. The Volunteers answered like a program that remembers every year of that drought. Kentucky's offense managed six points. By the time Tennessee stretched its lead to 20-6 early in the fourth quarter, the game was a formality. Safety Qua Moss forced two fumbles, Dejuan Lane picked off a pass, and every time the Wildcats reached for momentum the Vols' defense took it back.

The poll made it official. Tennessee, No. 16 before kickoff, vaulted seven spots to No. 9 with 1,177 points. That is 280 more than Kentucky, a gap that was a footnote on Friday and is a canyon now.

Elsewhere, the SEC has its king back. Georgia is No. 1 again at 8-1, with 1,729 points and 53 first-place votes, the clear choice of the room. Kirby Smart's Bulldogs climb one spot into the driver's seat and have Missouri next. Utah, unbeaten at 9-0, sits second with 1,675 points and 12 first-place votes, just 54 behind. Notre Dame is third at 8-1 with five first-place votes, and unbeaten UCLA is fourth. Miami, No. 1 a week ago, falls four spots to fifth at 8-1. Indiana is sixth.

The rest of the league is thick in the poll. Eight SEC teams are ranked, and a ninth, Missouri, collected 50 votes on the outside.

No. 13 Kentucky (7-2), home against Florida

No. 20 South Carolina (6-3), at Arkansas

Nobody in that group can look past the next game, and Kentucky least of all.

That makes Saturday night the one that matters. Florida comes to Kroger Field without a vote in this poll, unranked and unlisted among the others receiving votes. That is the kind of opponent that should be easy to dismiss and is dangerous for exactly that reason. A wounded team gets a visitor with nothing to lose, under the lights, in a stadium that has not been kind to anyone who forgot where they were.

Kentucky has to rebuild its margin, and it is thinner than it looks. The Wildcats sit 144 points behind No. 12 BYU and only 94 ahead of No. 14 Houston, which is 7-2 and not finished climbing. A poll is a rumor the voters agree to believe, and the rumor on Kentucky changes fast.

But a season is not one night in Knoxville, and Stein's team did not become a bad football team in the span of three hours. This is a group that went through a stretch of the schedule most programs would have signed for. It needs the same stubborn thing that built the 7-1 start: a clean week, a loud crowd and a first quarter that belongs to the home team.

Caturday night, in Lexington, is a good place to start.
authors: Lee Ann Herring Olvedo, UK Wildcats Wire

articles.title: Packers linebacker Ty’Ron Hopper questionable to return with chest injury
articles.summary: The Packers were thin at linebacker heading into Week 9 with the Patriots, and then suffered another blow as Ty’Ron Hopper is questionable to return.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, MA − The Green Bay Packers already are thin at linebacker, and that group took another hit early in the game with the New England Patriots.

Ty'Ron Hopper is listed as questionable to return with a chest injury. He briefly went into the blue medical tent.

Hopper as well as Isaiah McDuffie have stepped up at linebacker as Edgerrin Copper (Achilles) is out for the season and Zaire Franklin (shin) has missed the last three games.

Nick Niemann replaced Hopper during the second defensive series.

articles.title: What Deion Sanders said about his job security after Colorado’s loss in Tempe
articles.summary: The Colorado Buffaloes now have to win three straight games to play in December. A 20-10 loss to the Arizona State Sun Devils on Saturday night in Tempe drop...
articles.body:
The Colorado Buffaloes now have to win three straight games to play in December. A 20-10 loss to the Arizona State Sun Devils on Saturday night in Tempe dropped Colorado to 3-6 and 1-5 in the Big 12, and the path to six wins runs through the Houston Cougars at Folsom Field on Friday, a trip to the Cincinnati Bearcats and a home finale against the UCF Knights.

Colorado has lost six of seven since opening 2-0, and the one win in that stretch, a 27-24 overtime result against the Kansas State Wildcats, came the previous Saturday. The Buffaloes also extended a streak that has followed them all season: they have not won a Big 12 road game in two years.

Deion Sanders took up the season as a whole when he sat down with reporters afterward.

"The season don't look good. It don't look good. I'm not crazy. I can see clearly. You think I'm happy? I'm not happy with the outcomes. I'm not a loser by any means, and I hate the fact that we're coming up on the short end of these games," Sanders said.

How the game slipped away in the first half

Colorado did not pick up a first down until about seven minutes remained in the second quarter, and that drive ended with Isaac Wilson taking a 24-yard sack on fourth-and-6 from the Arizona State 34. Arizona State led 17-0 at halftime. Jake Fette threw a 34-yard touchdown pass to Reed Harris and caught a 1-yard touchdown pass, making him the first Arizona State quarterback since Jake Plummer in 1996 to do both in one game.

Colorado outscored Arizona State 10-3 after the break. Elliott Arnold hit a 39-yard field goal on the last play of the third quarter, and Wilson found Joseph Williams for a 7-yard score after Arizona State was flagged for running into the kicker.

Colorado's last chance ended on a failed fourth-and-15 near midfield with 2:43 to go.

Wilson finished 20-of-31 for 248 yards, but he was sacked four times and threw an interception, and Sanders measured the night against those numbers.

"You know, on a normal day, I would take that, but not the four sacks and the pick and everything else," he said.

Sanders was also asked about his own standing. Colorado went 9-4 in 2024 and is 6-15 since, and the question has followed him since a losing 2025 season.

"I don't think about that. I am not here for my job. I am not built like that. I am really, really not," Sanders said .

"I didn't see quit. I didn't see anyone being lethargic. I didn't see any giving up by any means," Sanders said of his players' effort. "But it was way too late."

articles.title: How Ducks did not shy away from Disney origins for Hometown Remix
articles.summary: What went into the 18-month process to design the bold green and purple threads, and why the team was comfortable straying from orange and embracing its movi...
articles.body:
ANAHEIM, Calif. – When the NHL unveiled all 32 of the league's Hometown Remix alternate jerseys on Monday morning, the bright pops of a green, purple and yellow color palette caught the eye of everyone getting their first full look at the Anaheim Ducks' entry.

It was an inspired reference to the team's origins and local culture that everyone could agree on, right Fanatics?

"Inspired by the fresh green of the parks we love to roam," the league jersey-supplier's press release said, "and the gold of our sunsets over the water, this jersey is an homage to the good life of Orange County."

You sure? You're certain it's not an ode to the District 5 Ducks uniforms of the 1992 cult classic Disney movie The Mighty Ducks –the namesake of the very NHL franchise on display?

If it walks like a Mighty Duck and talks like a Mighty Duck, well then "Quack, quack, quack, quack, quack Mr. Ducksworth," it's a Mighty Ducks jersey.

"They're certainly an ode to our past," Ducks chief marketing officer Meritt Tully said."That is pretty clear."

For the first time in their 33 years on NHL ice, the Anaheim Ducks will reach all the way back into their pre-history and don the same colors that Charlie Conway, Adam Banks, Connie Moreau, Lester Averman, Greg Goldberg and the rest wore today against the Pittsburgh Penguins at Honda Center. It's the first of 10 nights the team will wear the uniforms, including Tuesday against the Nashville Predators.

Leo Carlsson models the Anaheim Ducks' Hometown Remix uniform.

It was a bold decision for a franchise that turned fully into its "Orange Country" branding just two years ago, so how did these Hometown Remix designs come to be?

Tully explained that it was an 18-month process with the league and Fanatics, but even in that time there were only "small, minor changes" to the concepts Tully, Jillian Reddin–San Diego Gulls director of hockey operations and daughter of Ducks owners Henry and Susan Samueli–and other Ducks staff first saw.

The inception of this concept goes back even before that 18-month Hometown Remix timeline, when the Ducks and Fanatics were developing Anaheim's current orange-centric brand with the updated Mighty Ducks logo.

"We've talked about what are some of the things that we would want to bring into our color palette, as our brand begins its new evolution from when we rebranded a few years ago," Tully said. "We had conversations about when the time comes. Now, Hometown Remix wasn't a program at that point."

"We just knew that at some point, we're gonna want to really dive down deep into the history, celebrate the history of our franchise."

Now, 33 years in, when it comes to celebrating that history, there are varied and clashing looks to parse through. Again, although the team has never worn these exact shades of green and purple from the Disney movies, there are the original eggplant and jade classics, which transitioned into the black and gold Stanley Cup championship uniforms and again into the webfoot "D" logo with the larger inclusion of orange–not even including the various alternate sweaters.

As previously mentioned, for a team that has leaned all the way in on the orange in the last couple seasons, any change to a previous palette would provide a jarring juxtaposition, particularly the green.

"We talked a bit about that," Tully said. "We've rallied around a color in a significant way with that rebrand, and should that slow us down from, I'll call it creativity, and the ability to also incorporate elements of our brand that we know the fans would love? And in our minds, as we talked about it as a collective group, we don't want to stifle our fans' enthusiasm or creativity in the name of trying to be too rigid."

So, to break that form of rigidity, the Ducks and Fanatics went all the way back to where they've never gone before on the ice to suit up Anaheim in these District 5-inspired threads.

Charlie Conway as portrayed by Joshua Jackson in The Mighty Ducks (1992)

"We know we have a super unique history," Tully continued. "The only team that's born from a movie, right? And as we've looked over the past few years and just the fans kind of positive response to that history, as we've celebrated our 30th anniversary, and and then even beyond that our rebrand, we had a pretty good thought that people were gonna, people were going to like this, especially a certain set, were gonna like it."

That "certain set" brings up the elephant in the room whenever the Ducks produce a jersey of any kind, particularly one with historic nods.

It's the question asked by thousands across social media, whether they're on the nostalgia train because they lived it or because the '90s are trendy again: why won't the team simply wear true Mighty Ducks throwbacks?

"You're certainly gonna see the awesome part of all of these things is people have a passionate love for our organization," Tully said, "and they have thoughts on what they believe to be the right look and feel for who we are."

The last time the team wore full Mighty Ducks throwbacks was the 20th anniversary season, but it's not as if the team has shied away from the look while trying to serve multiple masters. The 25th anniversary featured an adjusted Mighty Ducks jersey with a black base and jade shoulders, and the 30th anniversary sweater was full eggplant and jade in a new design that included the old Wild Wing shoulder roundel as the crest.

Over the previous two league-wide Reverse Retro jersey initiatives, the team touched on that Mighty history with a white version of the 1996 Wild Wing sweater and an orange version of the original 1993 home sweater.

"For every time we do something that is an orange jersey, we hear that we should go back to the originals," Tully said. "You go back to the originals and somebody says that they love the orange or they love the old black or, hey, why don't they ever do the green?"

"I love the dialogue. There's certainly no end to it."

While the team is still fully committed to the color orange as they look to the future, there has been a more full and open embrace of the team's history over the last several years, especially as '90s culture has come back en vogue.

Even beyond the steady stream of throwback merchandise in the team store, Anaheim has done many activations with the movie actors–a few of which will be on hand Sunday and at future Hometown Remix nights–including bringing Joshua Jackson and Marguerite Moreau to the NHL Draft two summers ago to announce the selection of Roger McQueen.

Anaheim's chosen social media hashtag is #FlyTogether, referencing the inspirational intermission speech from D2– "When the roosters are crowing and the cows are spinnin' in circles in the pasture?!"

Heck, Disneyland is the team's helmet sponsor this year.

For a franchise that once dropped the Mighty name and the original color scheme in a deliberate break from the Disney era, this is all a pretty open embrace of elements that were derided as unserious or–in apt phrasing–"Mickey Mouse."

"If you've been around for a while, you remember the days where it wasn't always a positive thing to be a Disney owned franchise, and so it's really neat to kind of come full circle," Tully said. "I think of it like growing up. There's a lot of things that you do that are kind of maybe embarrassing when you look back in pictures at that, and when you grow up and you're old enough to have the confidence and enough in the rear view and mud on the tires, if you will, you can look back with that and enjoy the memories that there were, and embrace new ones."

The new memories can already include an overwhelming response to the Hometown Remix sweater, which saw the Ducks team stores highest single-day jersey sales numbers since the franchise's very first jersey sales in 1993.

They also move forward into the first of those 10 Hometown Remix on Sunday, which will have their own look beyond the jerseys on the ice and in the stands.

"I'm gonna leave a little bit to the imagination," Tully said, "but certainly, when it comes to the board and some of the entertainment elements, they will be catered to our Hometown Remix, the nights will have their own feel with the team and the way it looks. We're gonna change what the bowl looks like pretty significantly."

And for one last tease, fans can look to the skies on a future Hometown Remix night, as Fly Together may take on a new meaning.

"As far as our in-game elements, we're gonna be sure that we've got five ducks flying each of these games coming up," Tully said. "So we're excited about that. I don't want to give too much away, but we may have a special surprise, not Sunday night, but maybe a few hometown remix games from now with those ducks."

articles.title: Eagles lose a familiar advantage as Giants finally win at the Linc
articles.summary: The Giants won in Philadelphia for the first time since 2013, ending a 13-game road losing streak with a 19-11 victory over the reeling Eagles
articles.body:
For more than a decade, the Eagles could count on finding an advantage when the Giants came to Philadelphia. That stretch ended Sunday, another sign of how dramatically this season has turned. New York defeated Philadelphia 19-11 at Lincoln Financial Field, ending a 13-game losing streak at the venue that included a postseason defeat. The Giants had not won there since Oct. 27, 2013.

The result pushed New York to 5-2-1 and Philadelphia to 2-7. The Eagles enter their bye with seven consecutive losses, while the Giants leave with a road victory that had eluded them through years of roster and coaching changes.

Eagles cannot protect their halftime lead

Philadelphia led 8-6 at halftime after Saquon Barkley's 3-yard touchdown and Joe Milton's two-point conversion. Its defense collected five first-half sacks, preventing New York from building on two early field goals. That was enough to keep the Eagles ahead, but the offense couldn't build a meaningful cushion. Philadelphia scored only three points over the final three quarters and finished with 220 total yards.

The familiar home setting offered no protection from the offensive problems that have defined the losing streak.

Jameis Winston provides the decisive possession

New York's breakthrough came with its backup quarterback. After J.J. McCarthy left with a hip injury, Winston completed 6 of 8 passes for 71 yards and threw a 5-yard touchdown to Isaiah Likely. The 14-play, 76-yard drive consumed 7:56 and put the Giants ahead 13-8 late in the third quarter. McCarthy later returned, and New York added two fourth-quarter field goals.

Dominic Zvada made all four field-goal attempts, supplying 13 of the Giants' 19 points.

A rivalry result reflects Philadelphia's larger problems

The Eagles sacked New York's quarterbacks six times and limited the Giants to 80 rushing yards on 31 attempts. Those defensive numbers created an opportunity to extend the home winning streak.

Philadelphia could not take advantage. Milton absorbed seven sacks, the running backs combined for 28 rushing yards, and the final drive ended on downs.

The Giants did not need a dominant offensive afternoon to change the rivalry's recent history. They needed to remain patient, protect the ball, and capitalize when Philadelphia's offense stalled. For the Eagles, losing this particular streak was another consequence of failing to turn a competitive defensive performance into a complete game.

articles.title: Dave Portnoy wants Kyle Whittingham, Jason Beck fired after Michigan’s 15-6 loss to Michigan State
articles.summary: The Michigan Wolverines finished Saturday night with 192 yards of offense, a 2-for-10 mark on third down and four turnovers in a 15-6 home loss to the Michig...
articles.body:
The Michigan Wolverines finished Saturday night with 192 yards of offense, a 2-for-10 mark on third down and four turnovers in a 15-6 home loss to the Michigan State Spartans, a team that arrived in Ann Arbor at 2-6 without a Big Ten win.

Michigan did not score until the final two minutes and came within 1:35 of its first home shutout since 1967, per On3 . The Paul Bunyan Trophy goes back to East Lansing for the first time since 2021.

Dave Portnoy, the Barstool Sports founder and one of Michigan's loudest alumni, had run out of patience weeks earlier. After the 13-6 overtime loss to the Indiana Hoosiers in October, he told first-year offensive coordinator Jason Beck to "go get a plane ticket to the f***ing moon" in a video on X.

This time he widened the target and went after the head coach too, posting a two-sentence verdict on X after the loss: "Fire Kyle Whittingham. Fire Jason Beck."

Whittingham was asked about the Beck half of that demand at his postgame news conference, and his answer bought his coordinator three more games.

"Not right now. Not as I sit here at this podium, no. But, at some point, you've got to have results. It's a results-driven business, and it's a bottom-line business. But not right here, right now. I'll evaluate everything after the season and determine what the best course of action is," Whittingham said.

"Falls on me. I'm not hiding from that at all. Anything that happens has got my name on it," Whittingham said of the loss.

How far has Michigan's offense fallen under Jason Beck?

Beck followed Whittingham from Utah, and Michigan pays him a reported $3 million, the most of any offensive coordinator in the sport, Maize n Brew noted .

Against Michigan State, the running game averaged 2.1 yards per carry, and it was the third time in nine games that Michigan went to halftime without a point.

Whittingham moved off Bryce Underwood earlier in the season, and Underwood did not take a snap Saturday while true freshman Tommy Carr took the snaps. Carr threw two interceptions. The game's only Michigan touchdown came from running back Savion Hiter with 1:35 left, after the outcome was settled.

Portnoy's call for Whittingham's job goes further than anything the coach addressed at the podium, and the schedule offers little room to change the subject.

Michigan, now 5-4 and losers of four of its last six, plays at the Oregon Ducks next, then hosts the UCLA Bruins before closing at the Ohio State Buckeyes.

articles.title: “Everyone needs to look at themselves”: Patrick Dorgu does not hold back in scathing assessment after Aston Villa thriller
articles.summary: Manchester United produced trademark comebacks in both halves as they snatched a point late on after a thrilling 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday.The v...
articles.body:
Manchester United produced trademark comebacks in both halves as they snatched a point late on after a thrilling 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday.

The visitors scored twice within the opening four minutes of the first half, and it was left to Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans to restore parity before the break.

United's fortunes did not change much after the interval, as they ended up conceding twice within the opening eight minutes of the restart.

With Old Trafford emptying fast, substitutes Patrick Dorgu and Joshua Zirkzee combined to ensure a point apiece.

The Red Devils having to come back in every game is not sustainable , and Patrick Dorgu was scathing in his assessment of the team's situation after the match.

Despite the draw, the 20-time English league champions remain firmly entrenched in the relegation zone, something not many would have predicted at the start of the campaign.

"Of course it hurts [to be in relegation zone], there's a lot of games and we need everyone to come back sharp from international break and start getting wins."

Many inside Old Trafford, including the INEOS hierarchy, were delighted with the late point but not the Dane .

He even went so far as to say that the players have been underperforming and that they need to introspect and start fighting for the badge and the head coach.

"I don't feel happy – we are in a bad situation. We need to fight together to get out of it. Draw better than a loss but we had the better opportunities.

"Everyone needs to look at themselves and ask if they are doing enough. We need to fight for the manager, for the club and get out of this together."

Whether Carrick will be around for the Liverpool game after the international break remains to be seen, but INEOS will be well aware that plenty of the squad need to leave along with him.

articles.title: Commanders offense disappoints in 20-13 loss to Rams
articles.summary: Myles Garrett returns and wreaks havoc, leading the Rams to a 20-13 win over the Commanders.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders disappointed again on Sunday, falling to the Los Angeles Rams 20-13.

Trailing 20-13, Washington began its final offensive possession on its own 9-yard line after a Rams punt. Quarterback Jayden Daniels found wide receiver Stefon Diggs up the right sideline for 42 yards, all the way to the Rams' 49. The Rams' loafing to the ball was then penalized five yards for being offside, so the Commanders were now at the Rams' 44 with 31 seconds remaining.

Daniels then went incomplete, scrambled out of bounds for one yard, and on third down found Van Jefferson for 12 yards and another Washington first down at the Rams' 31. Two more incompletions followed, with Daniels setting up the final snap: a third-and-10 at the Rams' 31.

Daniels passed to tight end Chig Okonkwo, who made it to the Rams' 11 but then lateraled backward; after two scrambles, the Rams recovered at the 20 to end the game. With the win, the Rams are 5-4, and Washington falls to 2-5-1. Myles Garrett, returning to the Rams after an opening-game knee injury, was dominant, recording three QB sacks and forcing a Daniels fumble.

Rams receiver Puka Nacua schooled the Commanders' secondary all day with 14 receptions for 150 yards and the go-ahead touchdown, giving the Rams a 20-13 lead.

The Commanders had scored the first two times they had the ball, driving 11 plays for 48 yards and a Drew Stevens field goal for a 3-0 first-quarter lead. With the score tied 3-3, Washington drove 80 yards in six plays, scoring on Daniels 7-yard touchdown pass to Van Jefferson for a 10-3 lead in the second quarter. Earlier in the drive, Daniels threw 18 yards to Antonio Williams, then a 45-yard screen pass to Rachaad White, setting up Jefferson's touchdown catch.

articles.title: Worth the wait: Myles Garrett dominates Commanders in Rams return
articles.summary: In his first game since Week 1, Myles Garrett was unstoppable for the Rams, recording three sacks and a forced fumble in the win.
articles.body:
Nearly two months to the day, Myles Garrett finally made his return to the field for the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. It was his first game since the season opener in Australia, which was a major letdown to begin with. But after that loss to the 49ers, he said it was the "worst version" of himself that he could've put out there, lamenting his zero-tackle, zero-sack performance in Week 1.

In Sunday's 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders , he showed everyone what the Rams traded for.

Needless to say, his return after seven games on the sidelines was worth the wait. He finished with just three tackles, but all three of those tackles were sacks on Jayden Daniels. The first was a strip-sack when the elusive quarterback tried to escape the pocket, as Garrett knocked the ball out of his hands and it was scooped up by Omar Speights.

It didn't have the feel of a traditional sack, but it was a terrific play by the Rams star to force the takeaway.

His second sack was great, beating the left tackle to the outside before working back inside to corral Daniels before he could get away.

It's the type of play Garrett has been making throughout his career, bringing down even the quickest and most dynamic quarterbacks.

As if two sacks in his return weren't enough, he added a third for good measure.

On this one, he lined up as a stand-up rusher over the center, beat him with an NBA-style euro step and brought Daniels down for a huge loss. On the play prior, Garrett was flagged for jumping across the line early, so he more than made up for it with this sack in the fourth quarter.

Pro Football Focus ' grades and stats aren't finalized, but they illustrate how dominant Garrett was against the Commanders.

He was credited with a whopping nine pressures in only 30 pass-rush snaps, with three of those pressures being sacks. Garrett also landed another hit on the quarterback, giving him four for the game. As of now, his grade is an eye-popping 94.5, with a pass-rush mark of 94.6.

After the game, Garrett was asked how much this return meant to him.

"Honestly, it means so goddamn much," he said.

Garrett said he hasn't faced this kind of adversity before in his career, having missed the last seven games while rehabbing a knee injury that required surgery. It's not something any player wants to go through, but there's no question he looks significantly better now than he did in that opener when he was clearly not 100% healthy – something he admitted himself in Week 1.

If the Rams get this version of Garrett every week, and once they get Trent McDuffie back in the secondary, they're going to be a scary unit to face.

articles.title: Bo Nix throws for 2 TDs, Broncos win key challenge to beat Panthers 26-21 for fifth straight victory
articles.summary: (AP) — Bo Nix threw for 237 yards and two touchdowns and the Denver Broncos benefitted from a momentum-turning coach’s challenge to beat the Carolina Panther...
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — Bo Nix threw for 237 yards and two touchdowns and the Denver Broncos benefitted from a momentum-turning coach's challenge to beat the Carolina Panthers 26-21 on Sunday for their fifth straight win.

Jonah Coleman ran for 57 yards and a score and Courtland Sutton and Pat Bryant each caught TD passes for the Broncos.

Denver (7-2) got a late defensive stop as Nik Bonitto came up with a strip-sack on Bryce Young and recovered the ball near midfield with 1:24 left. The Broncos picked up one first down to seal the win.

Young finished 28 of 39 for 276 yards with three touchdown passes and an interception for Carolina. He was sacked three times after being sacked six times in a loss last week to Green Bay.

Darren Waller had eight catches for 90 yards and a touchdown for the Panthers (3-5), who have lost three straight.

The Panthers took the lead early in the third quarter when Young found Waller over the middle for a 15-yard touchdown pass.

The turning point came late in the third quarter when Broncos coach Sean Payton won a key challenge.

With Carolina facing a first-and-goal at the Denver 1, Young threw a pass toward the corner of the end zone that was initially ruled incomplete. After the Panthers had run a second down play, officials stepped in and said Payton had thrown the red challenge flag before the snap.

Upon review, officials ruled that Denver safety Devon Key had caught a ball that deflected off tight end Tommy Tremble's hand before it hit the ground. The interception gave the Broncos the ball at their 20 and ended Carolina's momentum and a chance to go up by eight.

Denver took advantage, going 80 yards in 14 plays to take a 19-14 lead on a 9-yard touchdown run by Jonah Coleman with 10:17 remaining. Denver's 2-point conversion pass failed.

Nix made it a two-possession game when he connected with a wide-open Bryant on a 25-yard touchdown pass down the seam with 5:41 left.

Young cut the lead to five with a 4-yard TD pass to Tetairoa McMillan with 3:05 left and would get another chance after the Broncos lost 18 yards on a misplayed pitchout from Nix to Coleman and were forced to punt with two minutes left.

But Bonitto's sack-fumble turned out to be the play of the game.

The Panthers played their first game under interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash, who replaced Ejiro Evero last week. But his defense, playing without its top four cornerbacks because of injuries, was flagged seven times, including five for pass interference.

Denver: Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and cornerback Riley Moss suffered concussions in the first half and were ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Denver: bye next week. Host Las Vegas on Nov. 22.

articles.title: Max Verstappen "needs to understand what happened" after "night and day" F1 comeback in Brazilian GP
articles.summary: According to Max Verstappen, the balance of his Red Bull car felt completely different after the first stint. The Dutchman stresses that he is very much look...
articles.body:
For the third year in a row, Max Verstappen has produced an impressive comeback drive in Brazil. While he won from 17th on the grid in 2024 and drove from the pitlane to the podium last year, Verstappen finished this year's Formula 1 Brazilian Grand Prix in second place after starting 21st.

His start did not go entirely to plan, however, as Verstappen acknowledged in the post-race press conference:

"To be honest, I had a very slow reaction time off the line because I was holding the clutch wrong. I had to very quickly react and then I was slow off the line, so that was my mistake," the four-time world champion admitted.

"Then I just got a bit unlucky in the first three corners where there was a traffic jam, three or four cars in front basically blocking how much I could pass. Actually, Lewis had a very good first lap, he could really get through those cars. I was a little bit disappointed that I couldn't make the same headway."

After that, however, Verstappen cut through the field like a hot knife through butter and soon managed to overtake his championship rival from 2021 as well.

"But then, within two laps, I was just flying by cars, almost every corner. We had a lot more grip, I guess, than most in the midfield. I don't know what lap I was in the top 10, but it all happened very quickly."

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing

Verstappen then continued his charge towards the podium positions and even appeared to have a potential shot at victory. After the first round of pitstops, however, the RB22 no longer felt the same, the Dutchman concluded post-race.

"As soon as I switched to the slicks, I had an extreme amount of oversteer in the car in the high-speed corners, which made it super difficult to drive," he said.

"We need to understand if something broke on the car, some kind of aero loss or whatever, because this was not normal. I sit here, of course, very happy with second, but at the same time, I know there was more in it if the car had been in good shape.

"Unfortunately, that was not the case. I actually did most of the race with a car that was not in good shape."

That was precisely why Verstappen immediately inspected the rear of his car after climbing out, to see whether there was any damage.

Red Bull had already acknowledged during the race that it could see a loss of rear downforce in the data, but at that point the team led by Laurent Mekies did not yet know whether, or where, the Dutchman might have sustained damage.

"But we have to understand why or what went wrong with the car as soon as we went to the slick tyres, because even when I switched back to the Inter tyres at the end, the car was night and day different to my first stint. That shows that there is something wrong," Verstappen said.

Nevertheless, climbing from 21st to second was still an impressive achievement, which also earned him the Driver of the Day award. Comeback drives at Interlagos have almost become a tradition, but Verstappen stresses that he would like to break that next year and ideally avoid a grid penalty in Sao Paulo.

"Maybe next year I'd love to start a bit further up front instead of starting from the back or the pitlane, but we'll find out next year," the current runner-up in the championship standings said.

"I like races like this, but next year, let's try and just start a bit further up front, please. That would be great to start with."

articles.title: Instant analysis of Colts' last-minute loss vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: With the clock at zero, here are our instant takeaways from the Colts' performance against the Cowboys.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts had a late lead over the Dallas Cowboys, but were unable to hold on, losing 27-23.

With the clock at zero, here are our instant takeaways from the Colts' performance.

Make that five consecutive losses for the now 2-7 Indianapolis Colts . When will the Colts find their next win?

That said, credit to the Colts' offense for fighting their way back into this game. Given how the season has gone, it wasn't a given that was going to happen.

After a dismal first half, with the passing game continuing to struggle, the Colts did string together two scoring drives in the second half and appeared to be positioned for a third before Jonathan Taylor's fumble. Spencer Shrader then added another field goal late.

Some redemption for Shrader. After missed kicks were costly a few weeks ago in Minnesota, he made two down the stretch in this game.

Another game where the Colts' defense gave up over 500 yards to an opponent.

The Colts' downfield passing game continues to be non-existent. While Ashton Dulin provided a spark with a 55-yard touchdown on a screen pass, the Colts' longest passing play otherwise was only 16 yards.

Not helping Daniel Jones is that it doesn't look like the wide receivers or tight ends are winning their matchups.

Josh Downs had what appeared to be two dropped passes.

Adetomiwa Adebawore continues to have an impressive season.

In other good news, rookie DE Caden Curry was in on two more big plays -- recovering a fumble and recording his first NFL sack.

Helping keep the Colts in this game were the Cowboys' own mistakes. Dallas was penalized 14 times for a whopping 153 yards.

The Colts' offense had five three-and-outs in this game, which contributed to the time-of-possession discrepancy between the two teams.

According to PFF's early tracking data, the Colts' pass rush pressured Dak Prescott on 14 of his 38 dropbacks. Indianapolis recorded three sacks and 7 QB hits.

It was again tough sledding in the run game early on, but the Colts did find some success late. Seth McGowan totaled 45 yards on six carries, with a long of 36 yards.

Cowboys' WR CeeDee Lamb had a big game, catching 10 passes for 195 yards and a score.

articles.title: Charles Leclerc penalised for Liam Lawson clash; Kimi Antonelli and Oliver Bearman also punished after F1 Brazilian GP
articles.summary: Charles Leclerc drops from seventh to eighth place in the final F1 Brazilian GP classification due to a post-race penalty
articles.body:
Charles Leclerc was handed a five-second penalty after the Formula 1 Brazilian Grand Prix for his clash with Liam Lawson , dropping the Ferrari driver down to eighth place in the final results.

The Monegasque was battling the Racing Bulls driver for seventh place on lap 69 of the Sao Paulo race when the pair made contact into Juncao, Turn 12, but both were able to continue and finish the race.

The clash did enable Leclerc to take seventh place from Lawson but the incident was placed under investigation for a post-race hearing.

After speaking to both drivers and assessing the video and data, the FIA stewards determined Leclerc was to blame and duly gave him a five-second penalty, dropping the Ferrari driver behind his rival and into eighth place in the final results.

The FIA stewards accepted that the contact was minor and in wet conditions, which was enough mitigation to keep the penalty to 5s and not a potential 10s punishment.

FIA stewards passages: "While the contact was minor and Car 30 was able to maintain the lead thereafter, the driver of Car 30 claimed that the contact damaged the rear left rim of his car and also enabled Car 16 to get closer to him on track and then eventually overtake him 5 corners later. Furthermore, under the Driving Standard Guidelines, Car 30 had the right to the corner and it was for Car 16 to take the necessary steps to avoid a collision.

"The driver of Car 16 claimed that it was a minor contact with no obvious sporting consequence.

"While we acknowledge that the contact was minor, having examined the fight on track between the two cars, we conclude that Car 16 was able to get closer to and thereafter overtake Car 30 because of the contact. The contact clearly disrupted Car 30 and allowed Car 16 to pull up alongside when it was further away before the contact. This was an obvious sporting consequence.

"In mitigation, the wet conditions coupled with the nature of the contact (i.e. minor) was taken into account in imposing a 5 second time penalty as opposed to a 10 second time penalty."

Antonelli and Bearman also penalised for unsafe releases from pitstops

New F1 world champion Kimi Antonelli was also given a five-second penalty after the Brazilian GP for an unsafe pitstop release.

The Italian was released from his final pitstop of the race into the path of the oncoming Franco Colapinto and despite attempting to take avoiding action it was judged unsafe and a five-second penalty was duly handed out.

But because Antonelli finished over 20s ahead of Oscar Piastri , who was directly behind him on the road, it does not change his final finishing position of fifth place – as Mercedes secured this year's F1 constructors' championship.

In a separate incident also involving Leclerc, Oliver Bearman was given a post-race five-second penalty for an unsafe release from a pitstop. The Haas F1 driver was released into the path of the Ferrari driver, which forced Leclerc to check-up in the pitlane.

The penalty has no consequence to Bearman either given he finished in 17th and one lap up on Sergio Perez in 18th place.

articles.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger’s Son Joseph Baena Places in Top 5 in ‘Pro Debut’ at Natural Bodybuilding Competition
articles.summary: The 29-year-old said he’s “extremely proud” of himself following the Nov. 7 event, which marked his third-ever bodybuilding show
articles.body:
Arnold Schwarzenegger's son Joseph Baena placed fifth in his category at the INBA PNBA Pro/Am World Cup on Nov. 7

The event was Joseph's third-ever bodybuilding competition, and he said it marked his "pro debut" in the PNBA

Joseph kicked off his bodybuilding career in the spring and has since called dad Schwarzenegger "the best training partner"

Arnold Schwarzenegger 's youngest son, Joseph Baena , just made his professional natural bodybuilding debut — and placed in the top five.

Joseph, 29, competed in the Classic Physique Open category at the INBA PNBA Pro/Am World Cup in El Segundo, Calif., on Saturday, Nov. 7, which he said marked his "pro debut" in the Professional Natural Bodybuilding Association (PNBA), which co-hosts the event with the International Natural Bodybuilding Association (INBA).

The son of Schwarzenegger, 79, and Mildred Baena came in fifth in his category at the competition held at the El Segundo Performing Arts Center. Joseph documented the event by sharing footage of his "posing routine" on Instagram .

Joseph — who began competing as a bodybuilder in March — reflected on the experience in a video shared on Instagram on Sunday, Nov. 8, stating that he is "extremely proud" of himself for placing in the "fantastic competition," and thanking everyone who supported him along the way.

He also shouted out his father, who was a professional bodybuilder before becoming an actor — and whom Joseph called "the best training partner" earlier this year .

"This was my pro debut in the INBA/PNBA — well, my PNBA debut — and it was for Classic Physique Open, and I placed in the top 5," Joseph said in the video. "So I'm extremely proud of myself."

Saturday's bodybuilding event marked Joseph's third-ever competition show, and the 29-year-old said he "came in looking so much better than last time," referring to an April event he competed in , which was the second competition of his career. It "was a very emotional day," he said of his latest go-around.

The burgeoning bodybuilder said he "felt good" up against the other pro competitors and called it an "incredible experience" for his professional debut show. He also revealed that his goal ahead of the event was to land in the top 5, which he achieved.

"I know what I need to do to improve," he said in the sit-down video. "I know what it takes to get better now."

Joseph also said in the video that he is "extremely proud of myself for the work that I put in," especially because he trained alone, with no coach. "Of course, there's guidance," Joseph said, "and, like my father always says, there's no such thing as a self-made man."

He did, however, shout out all of the "people in my corner," including his family and girlfriend, and everyone who has followed along with his bodybuilding journey via his social media posts.

Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories.

The latest milestone in Joseph's bodybuilding career comes months after he revealed in an April GQ interview that his dad helped kickstart his journey into the sport after he became interested in health in college.

"My dad gave me the bodybuilding encyclopedia," Joseph told the outlet. "I was flipping through that, trying to learn how to grow the biceps, and I fell in love with weightlifting," he continued. "I fell in love with eating healthy. I fell in love with learning about the body and how it reacts to training, and I became very passionate about it."

When asked what it was like to train alongside his famous father — the pair have been photographed working out together at Gold's Gym in Venice Beach, Calif. — Joseph told the outlet, "He's the best training partner. I don't know what to say."

articles.title: Studs and duds from New York Giants' Week 9 win over Philadelphia Eagles
articles.summary: Here's a look at the studs and duds (and those in between) from the New York Giants' 19-11 win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 9.
articles.body:
The New York Giants arrived at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday afternoon hoping to extend their NFC East lead over a Philadelphia Eagles team on a six-game losing streak.

In a rocky affair marked by several quarterback changes and struggling offenses from both sides, the Giants eked out a win over the sagging Eagles to improve to 5-2-1. It was Big Blue's first victory in the City of Brotherly Love in 13 games.

Here's a look at some studs and duds from Sunday's 19-11 victory over the Eagles.

The rookie put on a solid display, leading the Giants with 12 tackles (10 solo), with three sacks and a forced fumble. He is not only on his way for possible DROY honors, but he could also be making a bid for a Pro Bowl nod.

They looked out of sync all afternoon, with no push in the run game (2.6 yards per carry) and allowed nine QB hits and six sacks. When you don't win up front, you usually don't win at all. They were fortunate. Much room for improvement here.

No one expected to see Jameis in this game, but he provided much-needed relief when starter J.J. McCarthy was temporarily knocked from the game in the third quarter. Winston completed six of eight passes for 71 yards and the Giants' only touchdown, a 5-yard toss to tight end Isaiah Likely. He also rushed twice for 11 yards.

With Cam Skattebo (hamstring) inactive, Singletary served as the Giants' lead back in this game. He got very little traction, rushing for 31 yards on 21 attempts (1.5 YPC) and added eight yards on two receptions.

It was a perfect day for the embattled rookie, making all four field goal attempts from 53, 49, 38, and 49 yards, and converting his only point-after attempt.

McFadden had another strong game with nine total tackles, one for a loss, two QB hits, a sack, and a fumble recovery. The Giants are patting themselves on the back after bringing him back as a free agent this summer.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders’ failed two-point conversion seals Browns’ OT loss to Saints
articles.summary: Shedeur Sanders and the Browns' offense caught fire late in Sunday's game against the Saints, but Cleveland's fate came down to a two-point try.
articles.body:
A sluggish game between the Browns and Saints turned into one of the most exciting on Sunday's slate as both offenses started to catch fire late.

Shedeur Sanders, starting in place of an injured Deshaun Watson, managed two big-play touchdown passes in the fourth quarter and beyond, finding KC Concepcion for 64 yards in the fourth quarter and Harold Fannin Jr. for 39 yards in overtime, but the day came down to a two-point conversion for the Browns.

After coach Todd Monken opted to go for two rather than settle for a tie at best, Sanders and the Browns missed their shot to win.

Monken made the decision many coaches have making in this scenario, opting to go for two points and the win in overtime rather than attempting a game-tying extra point that would make a tie the best-case scenario for his team.

The risk, of course, is taking a loss that is worse than a tie. The Browns found themselves on the losing end of that bet on Sunday, as Sanders' pass targeting Denzel Boston was incomplete:

The play wouldn't have counted anyway, as Tytus Howard was called for holding. The Saints declined, but the Browns would have had to attempt a much more difficult play if the pass was complete to Boston.

The Browns' decision is understandable, but a tie would've been enough to push Cleveland into a playoff spot through nine weeks in the event of a Patriots loss on Sunday. By losing, the Browns will enter Week 10 out of the playoff picture at 5-4.

Sanders finished his first start of the season 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns, with the bulk of that production coming between the second half and overtime.

articles.title: Chargers vs. Texans: 5 takeaways from LA's loss in Week 9
articles.summary: The Chargers suffered their eighth straight loss. Here is a deeper breakdown of the Week 9 game against the Texans.
articles.body:
The Chargers are 0-8 after being thoroughly drubbed by the Texans by a final score of 44-22.

Here's what to take away from the latest embarrassing loss by LA.

Offensively, the Chargers continued to look completely lost. Moving coordinator Mike McDaniel to the booth did little to boost the worst offense in the league, and Los Angeles still looked like a team with no consideration of the details on Sunday. Tre' Harris and Oronde Gadsden II dropped passes in the first quarter. Justin Herbert threw an interception into double coverage (it was at least on a downfield shot). Keaton Mitchell dropped a carry and kicked it forward to negate a 50-yard connection between Herbert and Lambert-Smith in the second half. The Chargers' special teams had three players with an opportunity to recover a muffed punt and instead kicked the ball back into the arms of Texans punt returner Tank Dell. Even with Donte Jackson back from a hamstring injury, LA gave up 10.3 yards per pass before Stroud sat down, with Jackson frequently the culprit.

After Texans defensive tackle Sheldon Rankins put him on his back and chest, right guard Cole Strange was mercifully benched on Sunday, replaced by Branson Taylor, then rookie Alex Harkey. Rookie center Jake Slaughter continued to struggle and has remained unable to find defenders in space on the myriad of screens the Chargers run. Slide protection calls resulted in Charlie Kolar one-on-one with Texans edge rusher Will Anderson Jr., then tight end/fullback Scott Matlock on Jadeveon Clowney. Herbert was sacked eight times and did not finish the game because of a left-hand injury and the game state. The tip of Jim Harbaugh's spear is dull, as it has been essentially since the Chargers drafted Joe Alt in 2024.

41 points are the most the Harbaugh-coached Chargers have ever given up, and it came in a game where Houston was able to muster only 104 rushing yards on 3.7 yards per carry on the day. But Texans quarterback CJ Stroud threw for 384 yards and 5 touchdowns, including an acrobatic contested catch by star receiver Nico Collins. Dell burned Jackson on an out-and-up down the right sideline for a 63-yard touchdown, his first score since returning from a career-threatening knee injury 22 months ago. Stroud hit Kayshon Boutte over the middle for another 63-yard touchdown, where Boutte tightroped down the sideline and safety Genesis Smith made a not-so-aggressive effort to push him out of bounds. Houston scored a touchdown in all four quarters and averaged 8 yards a play before backup quarterback Davis Mills came into the game.

National reporting all week indicated that the Chargers were turning down trade calls unequivocally heading into this week, citing their belief that they can turn this season around. With the deadline coming up on Tuesday, attention will now turn to general manager Joe Hortiz as Los Angeles evaluates whether they still believe that. With the dearth of ascending talent at almost every level of the roster, however, it seems foolish not to entertain trading at least one veteran piece, whether that's edge rusher Khalil Mack, Jackson, or defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson, who are all on expiring contracts, to accrue a few more bites at the apple in the draft. At 0-8, what's left to salvage this season?

As the season creeps into November and the Chargers continue to hold the No. 1 overall pick in the draft, it seems fitting to provide fans with an update on superstar Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith until Los Angeles is able to squeak out a win. Smith led the Buckeyes with 7 receptions for 133 yards and a 13-yard touchdown catch in a 41-28 loss to No. 23 Oregon on Saturday despite Ohio State playing with backup quarterback Luke Fahey, a true freshman. Smith, should he end up in powder blue next April, should be used to the Chargers' brand of football when he arrives: the Buckeyes allowed 38 unanswered points after taking a 14-0 lead, a run broken by Smith's touchdown catch.

articles.title: Lions’ Dan Campbell reveals why Christian Mahogany got benched vs. Dolphins
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions took on the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon in their Week 9 contest. Detroit hit the field coming off a huge win over the Minnesota Viki...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions took on the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon in their Week 9 contest. Detroit hit the field coming off a huge win over the Minnesota Vikings the week prior. However, they had a bit of a different look on the offensive line.

Christian Mahogany, a third-year guard out of Boston College, was benched for this contest. There was no information given prior to the game about this decision. In fact, fans and media didn't know of it until the game began. After the win, Lions head coach Dan Campbell offered a clear explanation as to why Mahogany didn't play.

"That's team rules. That's what that is. Alright, so, it really is as simple as that. We have 70 guys, 69-70 guys, and they're all, we're all, expected to do it right, and when one doesn't, that's just the way it goes. It doesn't mean this is a done deal, it's just, he deserved that," Campbell said, via Brad Galli of The Brad Galli Show.

Overall, the Lions did enough to win this game. However, the offense didn't look great without Mahogany on the field either. Detroit gained just 270 yards of total offense on Sunday. Quarterback Jared Goff was sacked three times while failing to throw a touchdown pass in nearly two years.

Whatever Mahogany did to violate team rules is unknown. At this time, it appears this was a teaching moment for the young offensive guard. We'll see how the team and Mahogany move forward starting in Week 10 when the Lions travel to Munich, Germany to face Drake Maye and the New England Patriots.
