articles.title: Blunders on the Bay: Raiders cough up too many chances against 49ers
articles.summary: SANTA CLARA, Calif.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif.-- The last few meetings between the Las Vegas Raiders and San Francisco 49ers have taken on the vibe of a Super Bowl contender facing off against a team trying desperately to return to the ranks of the NFL's elite.

While the two teams are no longer in immediate proximity, the fires from the rivalry that once gripped the Bay Area every fall continued to burn bright. With the 49ers once again having legitimate Lombardi Trophy aspirations and the Raiders showing marked improvement from last year, the heat has only intensified.

It would take nothing short of flawless execution from the Raiders to return to Las Vegas with a statement win on their season.

Unfortunately, such a plan would never materialize, as the 49ers would take this latest chapter in the rivalry with a 38-17 victory at Levi's Stadium on Sunday.

At first, it was expected that the defense would be the unit that struggled to keep things together.

The run defense continued to struggle to the tune of surrendering five yards per carry, with most of the damage being done by Christian McCaffrey with 58 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries. Brock Purdy also put together an excellent first half with 123 passing yards and a touchdown, as well as adding another score on the ground.

The struggles at the beginning would lead to the Raiders giving up 30 points or more for the sixth consecutive game.

"We'll look at the film, and we'll make our decisions when we have cool heads," said Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak on if changes were coming to the defense.

However, the plot twist would come not necessarily in the way of the defense cleaning up, but in the offensive execution completely falling apart.

On the first offensive play of the second half, Kirk Cousins would mishandle a snap from Tyler Linderbaum for a fumble, then pick it up and throw it directly into the hands of 49ers linebacker Jaden Dugger for a touchdown.

It would be a prelude to how the remainder of the half would be played, as the Raiders were responsible for five turnovers in the second half alone.

Cousins would throw for three interceptions, while both Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer were responsible for fumbles that were recovered by San Francisco. Even though Treydan Stukes would record an interception in his own right for the Raiders, it was impossible for Las Vegas to come back with the offense continuing to turn the ball over and keeping the defense on the field for the majority of the time remaining.

While Cousins has typically been a bright spot even when games do not fall in the Raiders' favor, this is the first point in the season where he carries the brunt of the responsibility for a loss.

As a result, the fervor surrounding Fernando Mendoza will only continue to grow, and the Raiders will have to at least consider shortening the leash. While it was telling that Mendoza did not come into the game at any point, this feels like the first genuine point where a change is going to be considered. Whether the Raiders decide to give the first overall pick an opportunity is up for them to decide.

Regardless of whoever is in at quarterback, the Raiders have another challenging week ahead of them when the Seattle Seahawks continue their title defense when they enter Allegiant Stadium on Sunday.

articles.title: Game balls from the Saints' exhilarating overtime win over Browns
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints pulled off a 23-22 overtime victory against the Cleveland Browns thanks to incredible performances from these players.
articles.body:
In their fourth try this season, the New Orleans Saints finally got a win inside the Superdome with a 23-22 overtime defeat of the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. The Saints didn't make it easy on themselves. They blew two first half touchdown opportunities in the first half with questionable play-calling and a costly turnover. In the second half, awful defensive adjustments and nearly back-breaking coverage breakdowns nearly cost the win. Nevertheless, a gutsy performance by quarterback Tyler Shough and the best effort of the year from the New Orleans front seven pushed the Saints to 3-5 and a share of first place in the NFC South. Here were the players who had the biggest contribution to the win.

You wouldn't think that 72 rushing yards would earn a game ball, but Estime provided the best rushing threat the Saints have had all season. Released with an injury settlement at the end of training camp, Estime was re-signed by New Orleans after his release from the Browns this past week. He'd carry the ball 18 times for 72 yards, averaging 4.8 per carry and recording the team's highest rushing total of the year.

Estime got the first three carries of the opening drive. His 31 yards on those three plays surpassed the entire rushing total of 18 yards that the Saints had two weeks ago against the Steelers. Estime's effectiveness on the ground also opened up play-action for the Saints, something not often used by the offense this season.

Shough had an efficient first half, completing 7 of 10 throws for 135 yards, but failing to get the ball in the end zone. Included in that first half total was a big 52-yard throw to rookie Barion Brown and another big gain of 36 yards to Chris Olave. The first pass was squandered by a fumble at the goal line by Jordyn Tyson, but the pass to Olave led directly to a critical Charlie Smyth field goal before halftime.

Shough cooled considerably through the third quarter, but came alive again when the Saints needed him with the game on the line. He was brilliant on a 55-yard touchdown drive to take the lead late in the fourth quarter and the Saints 74-yard winning touchdown drive in overtime. On those two possessions, Shough completed 8 of 11 passes for 93 yards and a brilliant overtime touchdown pass to Juwan Johnson. For the game, he was 21 of 35 for 265 yards and a touchdown without an interception. Shough was also an aggressive runner, taking off 10 times for 51 yards on several crucial pickups. While there were questionable stretches, Shough outdueled fellow second-year quarterback Shadeur Sanders and continues to show that he is by far the best quarterback from the 2025 draft class.

A healthy Elliss makes a huge difference for the New Orleans defense. After missing three weeks with an injured calf and still being visibly slowed against Pittsburgh, Elliss was a ferocious force against the Browns. He led all Saints tacklers with 11 total stops, including 8 solo. Elliss also had a first half sack and several pressures, before coordinator Brandon Staley inexplicably stopped using him as a blitzer in the second half. Still, Elliss had several critical tackles short of first downs against the run and in coverage. His biggest play of the afternoon was a fourth down goal-line stuff of Browns running game Quinshon Judkins. Elliss, Chase Young, and Carl Granderson spearheaded the best performance of the year from the New Orleans front seven.

Young takes his familiar spot in this column, earning it on almost a weekly basis. He had a sack to bring his yearly total to 8 takedowns. Young drew a massive amount of attention from Cleveland blockers, yet still came through with several big pressures along with a tipped pass. While Young's production was again impressive, it was what doesn't show up on a stat sheet that was perhaps most important against the Browns.

Cleveland tight end Harold Fannin was his team's leading receiver but did not have a catch in this game until overtime. That is because the Browns were forced to keep Fannin on the line as an extra blocker against Young. Twice, Cleveland offensive linemen opposite of Young were flagged for false starts. Chase Young has developed into an elite force that affects offenses with his mere presence while still managing to be disruptive against extra attention.

While Chase Young and Kaden Elliss were defensive forces, Carl Granderson gets the primary Week 9 game ball for his performance against the Browns. Granderson had two sacks of Shadeur Sanders, his fourth straight game of at least 1.5 sacks. He had 7 tackles on the day, including some key run stops but not including a handful of vital pressures of Sanders. Granderson made the Browns pay for leaving him in some one-on-one situations while double-teaming Young. Cleveland never did find an answer for Granderson, who also drew a couple crippling holding penalties from Browns blockers. The most crucial was on the overtime two-point conversion attempt, and while Sanders threw an incompletion it still wouldn't have counted because Granderson was held. On a day where the Saints secondary failed them in big ways, Carl Granderson, Chase Young, and Kaden Elliss put out dominant efforts to pull out this win.

articles.title: Todd Monken "proud" of Shedeur Sanders, "not getting into" QB questions
articles.summary: The Browns fell short in overtime on Sunday, but head coach Todd Monken said he liked what he saw from quarterback Shedeur Sanders in New Orleans.
articles.body:
The Browns fell short in overtime on Sunday, but head coach Todd Monken said he liked what he saw from quarterback Shedeur Sanders in New Orleans.

Sanders was 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns, including a 39-yarder to tight end Harold Fannin that made it 23-22 in overtime. Sanders threw an incompletion on the ensuing two-point conversion, which allowed the Saints to escape with a win.

"I'm really proud of him and how hard he's worked since I've been here," Monken said. "He wasn't perfect. I wasn't perfect. But for a guy that really hasn't taken snaps with the ones in, what, 10 weeks. When we announced it with two weeks left and we're eight weeks into the season, so you're basically two-and-a-half months where you're basically running cards. To come in there and continue to battle, really proud of him."

Sanders got the start after Deshaun Watson missed most of the week in concussion protocol and Monken was asked if he made a case for a longer run as a starter during the loss.

"How long has it been? Thirty minutes since the game ended? I'm not getting into quarterback ," Monken said. "If we want to talk about Shedeur, we can talk about Shedeur."

Watson cleared the protocol on Saturday, but was inactive for Sunday's game. The Browns will host the Texans next Sunday and more clarity about their quarterback plans should come in the next few days.

articles.title: Denny Hamlin Reflects on Failing to Win 2026 Championship
articles.summary: Denny Hamlin finished third in the final NASCAR Cup Series points standings.
articles.body:
For the 21st year in a row, Denny Hamlin could not end the season as the NASCAR Cup Series champion. The driver of the No. 11 won the 2026 regular season championship after scoring four wins within the first 26 races.

When it got down to Chase time, the Joe Gibbs Racing star could not find the spark.

It seemed as if everything was working against Hamlin in the Chase. Hamlin failed to win through the 10-race period, lost the points lead to the eventual champion Kyle Larson after the third race of the Chase at Bristol, and could not keep pace with the No. 5 team when it counted.

Hamlin finishes the season third in the standings, 56 points behind Larson and seven points behind JGR teammate Christopher Bell, who finished second in the points.

Denny Hamlin on Not Winning The 2026 Championship: 'Definitely at Peace With This'

One year ago, Denny Hamlin was left devastated by the outcome of the Championship 4 race at Phoenix. Leading with three laps remaining, a caution followed by a deferring pit strategy put Hamlin behind. Larson took control of the championship lead and survived the final restart to win.

This year, NASCAR reintroduced the Chase format. Entering Homestead, it was going to take a miracle for Hamlin to pull off the championship.

Compared to last year's sudden shock of losing the title, Hamlin said he was able to stomach this year's loss a lot better.

"I feel OK. Knowing the outcome coming in made it way, way easier. It's not that 10-minute shock that was at the end of Phoenix [last year]. I was definitely at peace with this well before this weekend," Hamlin said.

Larson clinched the 2026 championship by finishing fourth in Stage 1 on Sunday at Homestead. Hamlin finished sixth in the stage and knew there was no stopping the Hendrick Motorsports driver from capturing the title.

"I went to a Virginia school but I could do simple math and could realize pretty quickly. … If he finished in front of me in one stage, that was going to be all she wrote," Hamlin said.

It might not have ended with a championship, but Denny Hamlin put together one of the best seasons of his storied NASCAR Cup Series career.

Hamlin captured four wins in 2026, with the first coming at Las Vegas in March. The 45-year-old out of Chesterfield, Virginia went on a summer hot streak with three straight wins at Nashville, Michigan, and Pocono, respectively.

The Michigan win tied Hamlin for ninth on the all-time wins list with the late Kyle Busch, who passed away two weeks before the win. Hamlin earned his 64th career win at Pocono to be the standalone ninth place on the all-time wins list.

Hamlin also won the regular season championship, clinching the top seed one race early in the regular season.

articles.title: Recap: Texans' offense ignites behind 5 TD performance from C.J. Stroud in win vs. Chargers
articles.summary: Not a bad homecoming for C.J. Stroud as the Houston Texans secured a much-needed win on the road.
articles.body:
Stroud, a native of Los Angeles, threw for a season-high 384 yards and tied his career high in touchdown passes with five as the Houston Texans rolled past the Los Angeles Chargers in a 44-22 victory at SoFi Stadium. Despite a slow offensive start, Houston found a rhythm in the second quarter and never looked back.

Stroud, who wanted to see an uptick in consistency after Week 7's overtime loss to the New York Giants , threw an early pick on a pass that was batted at the line of scrimmage. He missed Nico Collins on a third-down conversion and overthrew Marvin Harrison Jr. in the second quarter.

Outside of that, the former No. 2 overall pick looked like the quarterback that was promised back when drafted out of Ohio State in 2023. He connected with four different receivers, including twice with Kayshon Boutte for touchdown passes. Six passes went for gains of over 20-plus yards and were recorded as explosives.

The Texans punted with less than two minutes in the second quarter. Kai Kroeger would only take the field one more time for the rest of the afternoon.

For as good as Stroud was, the Texans' defense delivered a much-needed, jolt-worthy performance while attacking Justin Herbert. The Chargers' quarterback, who entered Sunday as the second-most-hit passer through eight weeks, took over at No. 1 as Houston's defense recorded a season-high eight sacks, including two each by Sheldon Rankins and Jadeveon Clowney.

Entering the third quarter, Los Angeles tried to get something moving in the passing game, but an interception by Derek Stingley Jr. stopped a chance for a scoring drive. On the flip side, Stroud found Nico Collins, who made an impressive one-handed catch for a 13-yard touchdown grab, only extending Houston's lead by 26.

But perhaps the best moment of the day came with Tank Dell's arrival back on the field. After missing nearly two seasons with a severe leg injury suffered in 2024, Dell didn't seem to miss a beat, hauling in four passes for 105 yards, including a 63-yard touchdown reception in the second quarter.

Entering the trade deadline on Tuesday, the Texans will have questions to answer about their future and the potential of moves that need to be made. But a win proves the season isn't dead. It's still far from trending toward a Super Bowl berth, but a 3-5 record could be the tool to ignite life in a promising roster entering the second half of the season.

The Texans hit the road next week to take on the Cleveland Browns at Noon.

articles.title: USI women’s basketball gaining valuable experience to start the season
articles.summary: USI women's basketball is now 0-3 after an 80-57 loss to No. 7 Louisville. Still, the Screaming Eagles remain confident going forward.
articles.body:
EVANSVILLE — The University of Southern Indiana Women's basketball team have learned valuable lessons in their opening week of the season.

No. 7 Louisville traveled to Liberty Arena to play the Screaming Eagles on November 8. It was the first meeting between the two teams in Evansville. They met in 2024 at the KFC Yum! Center — a 75-51 win for the Cardinals.

USI had its moments against Louisville, but not enough to keep the game within reach after the first half. The Cardinals won 80-57 and are now 3-0.

The Screaming Eagles, on the other hand, are 0-3. But their opening games have been against stiff competition.

"Obviously super excited to have a nationally ranked team come in," USI coach Rick Stein said. "All three games a really possession type games for a lot of it. I think we're improving daily, got a lot of production in a lot of different ways."

USI hosted MVC champion Murray State (82-67) on November 2 and traveled to Manhattan to play Kansas State (61-47) — one of the better teams in the Big 12.

But Louisville is on another level. Jeff Walz's group does not take possessions off — especially on the defensive end.

Their blend of ball pressure and rebounding ability was a factor throughout the afternoon. They also punished USI offensively for some of its defensive mishaps.

Momentum began to shift overwhelmingly in Louisville's favor after junior guard Imari Berry, the team's leading scorer, made a three-pointer at the buzzer to end the first half.

In the third quarter, the Cardinals outscored USI 26-12.

Still, Stein's group showed some resilience in the game — especially coming out of timeouts.

"You can't let a mistake roll into two or three or four, not with a team like this," Stein said. "I thought we did a good job of settling down and executing coming back out. I thought we lost some of our defensive identity in the third. But again, we bounce back in the fourth quarter and beat them 18-12."

The Screaming Eagles have earned a nice spark from center Channah Gannon. The sophomore leads USI in scoring to open the season with an average of 14 points per game.

Gannon faced a tough challenge in the frontcourt on November 8 with the size Louisville has, but she still found ways to create offense for herself inside. Gannon's ability to play inside and outside the perimeter has been a benefit to USI.

"It's not just me, I think all of our team is doing it," Gannon said. "Just knowing my role; getting an offensive rebound or scoring when the ball goes to me."

Gannon said playing the teams they have played will get USI ready in the long run.

Gannon shared the court with her sister, Chloe, at times against Louisville. Chloe, the team's second-leading scorer and rebounder last season, is still ramping up after an injury over the summer. After being sidelined for a month, Stein said Chloe returned too early and was out for another month.

Chloe started in the opener against Murray State but did not in the last two games. She came into the game averaging 19 minutes — sixth on the team.

"She's not 100% back to her strength or fitness," Stein said. "She's working her way back into that right now. Every single game, you're seeing a little bit more out of her."

The Screaming Eagles were dealt a tough blow when starting guard Tamara Ortiz went down with a left leg injury in the third quarter. Ortiz, USI's lone newcomer from the transfer portal, was carried off the floor unable to put any weight on the leg.

She left Liberty Arena on crutches and will see a doctor on Monday morning.

For a top 10 team to come into Liberty Arena is a good thing. The result was what it was, but it is another sign of the ambition this program has.

Stein's relationship with Walz extends back to their playing days — one that contributes to how the matchup was made possible.

Stein was at USI and Walz was at Northern Kentucky when the two went against each other on a couple of occasions.

They did not know each other then, but after the two programs met in 2024, Walz expressed a willingness to make the trip to Evansville.

"I did a double take," Stein said. "You're not going to see teams of that caliber coming to town, we got to generally go there. So appreciative of coach Walz, and believe it or not, before the game he said we might try it again."

Markos Tsegaye is a sports reporter for the Courier & Press. He can be reached at mtsegaye@usatodayco.com. Follow him on X @10_Markos_.

articles.title: Alim McNeill Sets Career Sack High in Lions Win
articles.summary: Alim McNeill cleared his own career sack best in Detroit's win at Miami on Sunday. #OnePride
articles.body:
Detroit Lions defensive tackle Alim McNeill had never recorded more than five sacks in an NFL season. He cleared that mark in Week 9, dropping Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis in the fourth quarter of a 19-9 Detroit win at Hard Rock Stadium.

McNeill entered the day with 4.5 sacks, a half-sack short of the five he posted in 2023. The sack of Willis at the Detroit 16 with 11:48 left in the fourth quarter moved him to 5.5 on the season , a new single-season best for him.

It came on the day the defense decided the game. Detroit sacked Willis three times and held Miami to nine points and 228 total yards, with every Dolphins score coming on a field goal. Defensive end Derrick Moore had the other two sacks, both of them in the fourth quarter as well.

Alim McNeill Is Having a Career Year for the Detroit Lions

McNeill also came into Sunday with 14 tackles and added three more against the Dolphins, which puts him at 17. The sack total is the number that travels, though: 5.5 in Detroit's eight games is a pace that would clear 10 across a full season, and the Lions still have nine games to play.

No Lions Defensive Tackle Has Reached 10 Sacks Since Ndamukong Suh

The last Detroit defensive tackle to put up 10 or more sacks in a season was Ndamukong Suh , who had exactly 10 as a rookie in 2010. Suh never got back to that number in Detroit either, topping out at 8.5 in 2014 before he left for Miami.

Detroit's defensive line has been the steady part of a 6-2 start, and McNeill is in the middle of it. He is not at 10 yet, but 5.5 through eight games is the best stretch of his six-year career, and if he keeps adding to it, a Pro Bowl spot is in play.

articles.title: Brent Venables praises John Mateer's 'fantastic' performance
articles.summary: Brent Venables praises John Mateer for his fantastic performance against Florida.
articles.body:
Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer had a first in his college career. For the first time, Ben Arbuckle didn't call the plays for Mateer and the offense.

Arbuckle was let go following the 42-25 blowout loss to the South Carolina Gamecocks . The Sooners have also been one of the worst offensive teams in college football the last three seasons. Tight ends coach Jason Witten was named interim offensive coordinator, and in his first game calling plays, Mateer performed well. He controlled the game, helping the offense total 351 yards and again didn't turn the ball over, which has been a big issue for him this season.

Head coach Brent Venables raved about Mateer's "fantastic" performance.

"Really strong performance by John," Venables said. "21-of-33, 207 (yards passing and) season-high 56 rushing yards... but, man, fantastic day for him."

Mateer's performance was an encouraging sign for an Oklahoma offense that desperately needed a spark. He protected the football, made plays with his arm and legs, and helped the Sooners maintain balance throughout the afternoon. Just as importantly, he appeared comfortable operating under Witten, giving Oklahoma reason to believe the coaching change can produce better results down the stretch.

The challenge now is building on that showing. Oklahoma needs Mateer to remain efficient and continue taking care of the football as the competition gets tougher. If he can sustain that level of play, the Sooners have a chance to finish the season with a much stronger offensive identity than the one that defined their struggles earlier in the year.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy ‘feeling pretty good’, aiming to be ready to face Washington Commanders
articles.summary: NY Giants QB J.J. McCarthy talks about coming back into the game and beating the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
For the first time in a decade, the New York Giants went into Lincoln Financial Center walked out winners.

The Giants topped the Philadelphia Eagles 19-11 on the road, rising to 5-2-1 on the season and dropping the Eagles to 2-7 in the process. It wasn't an easy game, and the Giants struggled to overcome the Eagles' defensive line as well as their own mistakes. But they did overcome them, as well as an injury to quarterback J.J. McCarthy that sent him back to the locker room.

But in the end it was McCarthy, and Jameis Winston, who ended the Giants' decade-long winless streak in Philadelphia.

"It means the world. The fact that [Jameis] and I got to do it, it's just a testament of what this team's all about," McCarthy said. "I can't thank the Mara's, the ownership, just the organization for putting this group together because it's a really special group. To get a gritty win like this and an environment like this and obviously the past was what it was, but to find a way to win, that's all that matters is going 1-0 every week and we did that today."

'Gritty' is probably the best way to describe a win that was in no way pretty, but they got the job done.

That also describes McCarthy, who left the field with a hip injury suffered on a read-option run.

"The play was quarterback-driven run, and I pulled it based on my read, and the goal is to get to the numbers, get out of bounds," McCarthy said, describing the hit. "I pulled it back inside and kind of saw bomb late and tried to get my shoulder down, didn't get it down enough and made a great hit. At the end of the day, I've just got to protect myself and do a better job of doing that."

"Football is a physical game," McCarthy said. "I can't thank the training staff enough for helping me get back on the field as fast as possible. But yeah, it's feeling pretty good."

He was only out of the game for one drive — a drive in which Jameis Winston went 6 of 7 and picked up two first downs with his legs — and returned for the fourth quarter.

"I feel good," he added. "At the end of the day, [as] I said, it's a physical game and a lot of guys are banged up, but we're going to do our best to make sure we turn over as fast as possible and do whatever we can between now and then and make sure we're as close to 100% leading up to a great opponent against Washington. They're going to be hungry, and we're really excited to go get this one."

After the game, head coach John Harbaugh said that McCarthy insisted on going back into the game for the fourth quarter.

"He insisted on it," Harbaugh said. "We weren't pushing him back out there. He was able to play, but he insisted on playing. Even at the end we thought about putting Jameis in there for the last drive and he insisted on being out there. It says a lot about him for sure."

"I think it means a lot because I think it just demonstrates the heart we're talking about," Harbaugh added. "Every single player has the opportunity to lead and demonstrate that at some point in time. And to your point, the quarterback is doing it and that's big. That's big to fight through that kind of thing, fight through an injury, go back in, take care of it, get back out there. Now he's going to have to fight to get ready to play on Thursday. That's part of it, too. So pretty impressive. Darn impressive. Very impressive."

McCarthy was certainly anxious and excited to get back into the game after coming out of the locker room.

"I'm able to walk, I'm able to throw. I want to get back out there as soon as possible," he said. "Just like I said, I can't thank the team enough – the athletic [training staff] for just really doing everything that was beneficial [to] me. They didn't really push any lines or anything like that, and I just can't thank them enough."

We all saw how fired up he was on the sideline after emerging from the locker room.

"I feel like it was definitely a moment where it was one of those things where you have to make that decision," he said. "At the end of the day, no matter what, it's about my brothers and I'll do whatever I can to help them the best I can to be successful. And I felt like I was able to do enough to make sure that we could move the ball. Obviously, yes, put it all on the line for this organization and everything I can to help go get a win."

And McCarthy helped the Giants get the win, and he could feel the tide shift as the Giants pulled out to a two-score lead.

"It was amazing," McCarthy said. "You could just feel the passion and the excitement and the desire to win from the entire fan base. It gives us so much motivation out there. I was telling the guys in the huddle, 'Look around, see that blues are starting to fill up more than green." It just gives us that much more juice to go out there and execute that next play. I can't wait to see the home fans Thursday night and be able to really give them a show because offensively we've got to do a better job with the defense playing fantastic today. Special teams played fantastic and we're excited to make it right."

articles.title: UND answers season-opening loss with win over Minot State
articles.summary: Nov. 8—GRAND FORKS — UND head coach Dennis Hutter made it clear that last Monday's loss to Minnesota Crookston fell short of "the standard we're trying to se...
articles.body:
Nov. 8—GRAND FORKS — UND head coach Dennis Hutter made it clear that last Monday's loss to Minnesota Crookston fell short of "the standard we're trying to set here."

The Fighting Hawks' 84-68 win over Minot State Sunday afternoon at the Betty Engelstad Sioux Center was much closer to the framework Hutter and his coaching staff are trying to build in Year 2, though it wasn't perfect.

"I'm happy they won, I like this team a lot," Hutter said. "I think they play hard, they compete, they're invested in the program, they're invested in each other. I think that goes a long way, so I believe they deserve to have some success. It's nice to bounce back a little bit tonight. Not sure how clean it was, especially toward the end there a little bit. Again, one of the things people ask me is, 'How do you get a team to win?' And I'm like, the first thing you've got to do is they've got to be in a winning situation. They've got to learn how to hold a lead, how to play with the lead in the fourth quarter. We have a new group, and we didn't get a chance to do that the other night, so it was nice to see them learn how to play with the lead a little bit."

The Hawks scored 22 fastbreak points and showed better ball movement offensively, finishing with 17 assists on 28 made baskets. Junior guard Ciona Wells hit a jumper on the fastbreak to give UND a 14-12 lead with 3:32 left in the first quarter, and the Hawks led the rest of the game.

The Hawks' lead ballooned in the second half. They led by as many as 24 points in the fourth quarter, though Minot State went on a 12-4 run to close the game.

"I thought we had some moments of what we're looking for," freshman Jayden Sonnenberg said. "We had a lot of good transition and (forced) a couple shot clock violations, and that's what we're looking for as a team. But I think the next step is just stringing that together and having four quarters, not just one or two or a little bit here and there. We need to be able to come together and put a full game together."

Jayda Maves had a major bounce-back performance after shooting 1-for-15 against Minnesota Crookston. The senior guard scored a team-high 19 points against the Beavers, going 9-for-17 from the field.

"I just have this support system through teammates and coaches," Maves said. "Whether my teammates get on me, or my coaches get on me, I just respond very well. That's something that I've grown to learn how to do. And even if my shot's not falling, I'm was like, 'Just drive, just get in there,' and I have no fear anymore."

Maves shot 1-for-6 from 3-point range but found success with quick drives and finishes at the rim.

"Jayda can do a lot of different things," Hutter said. "Jayda's got explosiveness. She's quick, she's fast, handles the ball well, scores on both sides of the rim. She hasn't shot it to a level that I think she would be comfortable with; she hasn't shot it very well, not to the Jayda standards that we have seen in practice. That will come, like we talked about today, especially early — I'm like, 'Jayda, you've got to stop being a shooter, we need you to be a scorer now. You've got to find ways to score: getting downhill, getting to the free-throw line, scoring in transition, scoring out of your defense, just different ways to score.'"

Sophomore London Harris added 14 points, while Wells finished with 11. UND's bench contributed 32 points, led by Sonnenberg's 13.

The Hawks were also better defensively, holding Minot State to 41% from the field. Junior forward Lara Dobbins and senior guard Taryn Hamling were the Beavers' two biggest threats; Dobbins scored 21 and Hamling finished with 18.

Hutter, however, still hopes to see more out of the defensive effort.

"It was a little better, not where it needs to be," Hutter said. "I just feel like we're not physical enough. The word I've been using all week is resistance. I just don't think we play with a tremendous amount of resistance. We have to find a way to defend the ball at, let's say, 22 feet, and not let it get down to 12 feet, something along those lines. I just felt like there were times that we're holding them up, we're holding them up, and they turn the corner on the last dribble and get themselves there."

UND improved to 1-1 on the season. The Hawks will now take to the road for two games, beginning with Milwaukee on Thursday.

"It's another challenge, it's another thing we haven't done," Hutter said. "Before we played Crookston on Monday night, we said, 'We haven't played a game, we don't know how we're going to handle a competitive situation, because we haven't had one yet.' Same thing can be said for on the road. We haven't played on the road, we haven't really traveled, so it's another challenge that we have to work through to find out what kind of team we have. I do believe that connected teams have the ability to win on the road, they really do, so I just feel like it's a great opportunity for us to build off tonight and take it onto a new setting."

articles.title: Maloney volleyball wins CCC tournament championship over Southington
articles.summary: Maloney volleyball wins CCC tournament championship over Southington.
articles.body:
Greta Koscuk produced 27 kills and 25 digs to lead the Maloney volleyball team to its first Central Connecticut Conference tournament championship in program history, winning 3-1 against Southington on Saturday night at the UConn Volleyball Center in Storrs.

Set scores were 24-26, 25-15, 25-23, 25-19.

Maloney (22-2) entered the tournament as the No. 2 seed, and beat No. 15 Hall 3-0 in the first round, No. 10 Enfield 3-0 in the quarterfinals and No. 3 Bristol Central 3-1 in the semifinals. Maloney had previously never appeared in a CCC volleyball championship until their win on Saturday.

Southington, the No. 1 seed, won 3-0 against No. 16 Rocky Hill in the first round, 3-1 against defending champion No. 9 Simsbury in the quarterfinals and 3-2 against last year's runner-ups No. 4 Glastonbury in the semifinals.

Tessa Holmes followed with 44 assists, 11 digs and three aces for Maloney.

Maloney heads into the CIAC Class LL tournament as the No. 2 seed with a first-round bye, awaiting the winner of No. 18 Simsbury and No. 15 Newtown.

Southington enters the Class LL tournament as the No. 4 seed and will face No. 29 New Britain in the first round on Tuesday at 6 p.m. at home.

articles.title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs fractures finger on right hand in win over Patriots
articles.summary: Packers RB Josh Jacobs fractured a finger on his right hand during Sunday's win over the Patriots.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs fractured a finger on his right hand and was unable to return to Sunday's win over the New England Patriots.

Coach Matt LaFleur said Jacobs didn't return because he wasn't able to fully grip the football.

"He fractured a finger. Hopefully we can do something to allow him to go out there, but he was having a hard time gripping the ball," LaFleur said post-game.

Jacobs appeared to fracture the finger while attempting to stiff-arm a defender at the end of a run in the first quarter. He went back to the locker room for evaluation and eventually returned to the sideline but was unable to get back into the game. Several times, the TV broadcast showed Jacobs tried to work through the injury on the sideline. It appeared catching the football also created pain in the broken finger.

Jacobs confirmed the injury in the post-game locker room:

Jacobs rushed four times for five yards before the injury.

The Packers used Pierre Strong Jr. and Kaleb Johnson at running back the rest of the way. The pair combined for 90 rushing yards, including 68 from Johnson, and the Packers finished with a season-high rushing total of 129 yards.

The Packers face the Minnesota Vikings at Lambeau Field next Sunday.

articles.title: Seahawks QB Drew Lock suffered oblique injury in win over Cardinals
articles.summary: Drew Lock's status for Week 10 vs the Raiders is now in question.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks ' quarterback room is the walking wounded these days. Seattle was forced to turn to backup Drew Lock on Sunday with regular starter Sam Darnold sidelined with a quad injury and cracked rib. Lock was banged up himself with "severe tendinitis" in his throwing elbow per NFL insider Tom Pelissero . Unfortunately, Lock wasn't able to escape cleanly.

During the Seahawks' 17-3 win over Arizona, Lock apparently suffered an oblique injury according to head coach Mike Macdonald. His status for Seattle's Week 10 game against the Las Vegas Raiders is now in doubt. If Lock cannot go in Week 10, one begins to wonder who exactly the Seahawks are going to start, because Sam Darnold's status for the Raiders game is also in doubt.

If there is any hope to be found, Drew Lock himself said he feels confident he will be ready to go for next week's game. Lock was asked about it during the postgame press conference and answered in the affirmative.

Lock played his usual efficient self, continuing his streak of keeping the Seahawks undefeated when he's under center. The former Mizzou standout was 19-of-28 for 175 yards and a touchdown. Although those numbers aren't exactly eye-popping, Lock did more than enough to keep Seattle's offense moving and taking full advantage of the Dark Side's dominance. Most importantly, Lock did not turn the ball over once, and the Seahawks' offense played a clean game.

If Lock is unable to go, all eyes turn to second-year quarterback Jalen Milroe.

articles.title: Dak Prescott throws for 335 yards, two TDs in Week 9 comeback win
articles.summary: Dak Prescott tied a season with 335 yards passing and added a pair of passing TDs as Dallas rallied late to beat Indianapolis.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott completed 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns in Week 9 against the Indianapolis Colts . He ran two times for one yard and lost a fumble.

Why It Matters: Prescott matched his season-high in passing yards while topping 300 yards for the third time this season and engineered a game-winning drive in the final minutes to secure the win. Prescott got the ball down the field in this one (9.9 yards/attempt) after averaging a career-low 6.8 entering the contest. He's thrown a TD pass in all nine games this season but has multi-TDs in just four games. He's a low-end QB1 option in most formats, including in Week 10 against what has been a better-than-expected 49ers defense.

articles.title: Ryan Blaney steals Homestead win as Kyle Larson claims NASCAR Cup title
articles.summary: By Reid Spencer NASCAR Wire Service HOMESTEAD, Fla. — Ryan Blaney stole the consolation prize from Tyler Reddick with two laps left in Sunday’s NASCAR Cup Se...
articles.body:
HOMESTEAD, Fla. — Ryan Blaney stole the consolation prize from Tyler Reddick with two laps left in Sunday's NASCAR Cup Series Championship Race at Homestead-Miami Speedway, but it's Kyle Larson who will leave South Florida with the championship trophy.

Blaney passed Reddick on Lap 266 of 267 in the final race of the reconstituted NASCAR Cup Series Chase presented by Mobil 1 and powered his No. 12 Team Penske Ford across the finish line 0.314 seconds ahead of the Reddick's 23XI Racing Toyota.

Long before Blaney secured his fourth victory of the season and 21st of his career, Larson had clinched his second straight championship and third overall with a fourth-place finish in the first stage.

After multiple brushes with the outside wall, Larson eventually rolled home in 12th in the No. 5 Hendrick Motorsports Chevrolet, becoming the first Cup Series driver to win back-to back titles since Hendrick legend Jimmie Johnson claimed five straight from 2006 through 2010.

"I got word that we clinched it, and I started driving like an idiot," Larson said with a laugh.

Larson became the 11th driver to win three or more championships in NASCAR's top division. As broadcaster Jeff Burton pointed out earlier in the weekend, more humans have walked on the moon (12) than have won three Cup titles.

Larson joined an elite group of three-time champions that includes NASCAR Hall of Famers Lee Petty, David Pearson, Darrell Waltrip, Cale Yarborough, Tony Stewart and current Team Penske driver Joey Logano.

The championship was the 16th for team owner Rick Hendrick, extending Hendrick Motorsports' series record.

"I'm just so proud of my team, first and foremost," said Larson, who finished 49 points ahead of second-place Christopher Bell and 56 in front of third-place Denny Hamlin. "Hendrick Motorsports, this was statistically probably one of our worst years. To still come away with the championship shows how resilient everybody at the race shop is, everybody on my 5 team, all my teammates, 24 (William Byron), the 9 (Chase Elliott), the 48 (Alex Bowman). GM (General Motors), too, Chevrolet, all the key partners there.

"We absolutely could not have done what we did in the Chase without the teamwork that it took. That's what this championship is, makes it so meaningful, just the teamwork. This one more than any of them took teamwork."

Larson's third championship was official when pole winner Chase Briscoe's engine blew on Lap 78, ending the first stage. Larson was running fourth at the time, one position behind Bell, with Hamlin in sixth.

By scoring seven stage points to Bell's eight and Hamlin's five, Larson put the title mathematically out of the reach of his Joe Gibbs Racing pursuers. Hamlin and Bell were left to battle for second place in the final standings.

"They've declared it—we've got it," crew chief Cliff Daniels radioed to Larson during the caution. With his third championship—all with Larson—Daniels is tied for fourth all-time among Cup Series crew chiefs.

"Like it's done—over?" asked Larson, just making sure. "That was a little anticlimactic, but that's cool. Good job, guys!"

Hendrick radioed his delight to the 34-year-old driver from Elk Grove, California.

"Congratulations," Hendrick said. "Now you can run the wall."

That's exactly what Larson did, but the freedom came with a price. On Lap 119, Larson steered the No. 5 Camaro to pit road with a cut right rear tire—the result of contact with the outside wall.

Larson's trip to the pits started a green-flag cycle, with Bell following from the race lead eight laps later and Reddick right behind him. But it was Hamlin, who pitted three laps earlier than Bell, who grabbed the lead and held on to win the second stage, as Larson faded to 17th on well-worn rubber.

Blaney's journey to the checkered flag was convoluted, to say the least. During the first stage break, he returned to pit road to remedy a loose wheel and restarted at the back of the field. By the end of Stage 2, he had climbed to fifth in the running order.

In the final stage, Blaney ran long and pitted on Lap 220 and was running down Byron and Reddick from five seconds back when a caution bunched the field and set up a restart with eight laps left.

Blaney restarted fourth, passed Bell on lap 263, slipped past Byron a lap later and made the winning pass of Reddick on Lap 266 of 267.

"Pretty cool night battling back from coming down pit road," said Blaney, who avenged a haunting last-lap loss to Reddick at 1.5-mile Homestead in 2024. "Car was really, really fast. I appreciate everybody for sticking with it.

"Even though we weren't part of the championship fight, our goal was to try to win the race, end on a high note, get the most points we can."

The victory elevated Blaney three positions to fourth in the final standings, 94 points behind Larson.

Byron, who was leading by just over one second when Noah Gragson spun Daniel Suarez in Turn 1 to cause the third and final caution with 14 laps left, finished third in front of Bell and Bubba Wallace.

Hamlin came home sixth, followed by Austin Cindric, Suarez, Gragson, and Michael McDowell.

Bell and Hamlin were the only two drivers still mathematically alive for the title entering Sunday's race, but winning would have required a perfect night from one of the two JGR drivers along with calamity for Larson.

"This year consistently we were in the mix," Bell said. "We were in there for contention of race wins. Obviously disappointed we didn't win more. Yeah, just happy and thrilled and thankful that I'm in position.

"Something to build on. Hopefully, we can execute a little bit better and get that grand prize at the end."

A four-time winner this season, Hamlin echoed Bell's sentiments.

"We had a great year," he said. "Every way you can measure the year, it's been really, really good. Congrats to the 5 team. They deserve everything, the spoils of victory. They performed absolutely incredible during these last 10 races.

"We are extremely happy with the 36 races that we put together. It's really tough to do in this sport. Certainly felt good to be competitive from the first race to the last."

Notes: Hamlin led a race-high 87 laps, followed by Reddick with 53, Bell with 46 and Byron with 38. Blaney led seven laps… J.J. Yeley finished 36th in his 400th Cup start, one spot ahead of Casey Mears, who achieved his personal goal of 500 Cup starts… Justin Haley ran 21st, subbing for suspended Spire Motorsports driver Carson Hocevar.

articles.title: Highlights of Packers' 45-27 win over Patriots in Week 9
articles.summary: Miss the Packers' Week 9 victory over the Patriots on Sunday? We have you covered with highlights and post-game press conferences.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers got four total touchdowns from Jordan Love and four takeaways from Jonathan Gannon's defense to power a dominant 45-27 win over the defending AFC champion New England Patriots on Sunday at Gillette Stadium.

Love was magnificent, throwing for 372 yards and three touchdown passes while rushing for a score and not having a turnover. The Packers picked off Drake Maye three times and scored 22 points off takeaways. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden produced 335 total receiving yards, while Xavier McKinney created two interceptions and Karl Brooks finished with two sacks.

The win improved the Packers to 6-3 after nine games, an impressive mark considering the team's 1-2 start.

articles.title: Caleb Williams TD pass gives Bears early 7-0 lead
articles.summary: It took a couple of attempts, but Caleb Williams and Rome Odunze connected for a score on Chicago’s opening drive to take a 7-0 lead over Tampa Bay.
articles.body:
It took a couple of attempts, but Caleb Williams and Rome Odunze connected for a score on Chicago's opening drive to take a 7-0 lead over Tampa Bay.

It's Williams' seventh passing touchdown of the season, as the young quarterback looked sharp on the Bears' first set of plays.

He moved the chains with a 7-yard scramble on third-and-6. Then he got another first down with his legs with a 4-yard scramble.

A pass to receiver Zavion Thomas put the Bears on the 13-yard line. While Odunze originally appeared to have brought in a 13-yard touchdown over the middle in the end zone, he had actually bobbled the ball and didn't secure possession until he was out of bounds.

So, after a D'Andre Swift 4-yard run, Williams went to Odunze again on third-and-6. This time, a wide-open Odunze slid and caught it for his first receiving touchdown of the season.

articles.title: Five grabs for Malik Nabers in Week 9
articles.summary: New York Giants WR Malik Nabers targeted eight times against Philadelphia
articles.body:
New York Giants WR Malik Nabers caught five of is eight targets for 43 yards against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 9.

Why it Matters: Nabers saw his streak of four straight 100-yard receiving games come to an end, but he still caught at least five passes for the seventh time in eight games. After a slow start to the year, Nabers has become a steady force for the Giants' offense. Consider him a WR2 with upside.

articles.title: Texans report card: Grading Houston's dominant victory over the Los Angeles Chargers
articles.summary: The Houston Texans dominated the Chargers as C.J. Stroud passed for five touchdowns and the defense had eight sacks. Grading the performance.
articles.body:
Turns out, a week off was just what the Houston Texans needed.

They dominated the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium, 44-22, improving their record to 3-5.

Here are the grades from the performance:

Even with the interception he threw, it was difficult not to give C.J. Stroud the highest score possible. He tied a career-high with five touchdown passes and threw for a season-high 384 yards.

It was hands down his best performance of the season, and it came against a good Chargers defense. The Chargers had given up only eight passing touchdowns heading into this game.

But they got exposed by Stroud. He finished 21-of-35 for 384 yards, five touchdowns and the one interception.

The Texans still haven't had a big game running the ball since the first game of the season, but Woody Marks was decent against the Chargers' defense. Marks finished with a season-high 70 yards on 18 carries, averaging 3.9 yards per carry.

Stroud added 20 yards rushing on two carries, and backup Emari Demercado had 16 yards on six carries. Together they ran for 116 yards.

Running back David Montgomery should be close to a return from a groin injury. His return should help the running game, but even then Marks should remain the starter.

The story of the day was Tank Dell's impact. He had a 63-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter that gave Houston a 17-9 lead. He finished with four catches for 105 yards in only his second game in two years since returning from a major knee injury.

But he wasn't even the one who led the team in receiving yards. Kayshon Boutte had his best game as a Texan, finishing with four catches for 125 yards and two touchdowns. Nico Collins had four catches for 55 yards and a touchdown. Tight end Dalton Schultz had two catches for 42 yards. And Xavier Hutchinson had three catches for 29 yards and a touchdown.

This is what Houston envisioned when it went out and got all of these receivers - a balanced attack that would make it difficult for defenses to key in on Collins.

Stroud was sacked just once. He had time in the pocket, which is why he was able to be so effective. The offensive line was also able to open up holes for the running backs.

The Texans rushed for 114 yards on 28 carries, including the two kneel downs by Davis Mills at the end of the game. It was the third time this season that the Texans' running game went over 100 yards rushing. And this was against a good Chargers defense.

This was arguably the best game for the Texans' defensive line. They finished with a season-high eight sacks, including two from Will Anderson Jr., two from Sheldon Rankins, and two from Jadeveon Clowney.

Anderson came into Sunday's game tied for the league lead with 7½ sacks despite not having any in his previous two games. He should remain at the top.

Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert was in a state of disarray all day. He finished 13 of 23 for 193 yards, one touchdown and an interception.

It was a much better game for Azeez Al-Shaair and Henry To'oTo'o, who were all over the field and didn't miss many tackles compared to previous games although there were still a few missed. To'oTo'o got into the backfield for two important tackles for loss. Al-Shaair led all defenders with nine tackles.

Overall it was a better performance and was why the defense was more effective.

Derek Stingley Jr. did pick up his first interception of the season, and Herbert threw for less than 200 yards. But Stingley also gave up a 50-yard passing touchdown, continuing a trend of this defense giving up explosive plays.

Calen Bullock also got his hands on balls and nearly came down with an interception of his own. And Jalen Pitre delivered some big tackles.

Kicker Ka'imi Fairbairn, who was named AFC special teams player of the month for October, knocked in all three of his field-goal attempts. Kai Kroeger shanked a punt and didn't help the defense much with field position. And Tank Dell muffed a punt, though he later recovered it.

The Chargers scored 22 points against the Texans, though two touchdowns came in garbage time.

But the offense put on its best performance with a season-high 41 points. They couldn't be stopped.
